title: The Stand-in Bride Marries into the General’s Household
author: Yu Dan Feng Qing
synopsis:
In her past life, Yu Qingci refused to be a stand-in bride and was schemed by her stepmother into marrying a wolf in sheep’s clothing. After ten years of suffering, she perished alongside her in-laws. 

Reborn, Yu Qingci decides to accept the proposal to marry into the General’s Household as a stand-in for her elder sister, guarding the widow’s door. For she knows that in three years, the young general, rumored to have died in battle, will return safely.
The General’s Household rapidly declines after losing two generations of generals. 

After marrying in, Yu Qingci outsmarts her shameless relatives, protects her weak mother-in-law and sister-in-law, uses her past life’s memories to do business and accumulate wealth, and single-handedly revives the General’s Household.

Three years later, Young General Lu Yunqi returns with his confidante, earns great merits, and is honored by the court. The General’s Household soon regains its former glory...

chapters.title: The Concubine Enters the Household
chapters.content:
"Qingci, Lian’er is your half-sister. Marrying her as a concubine was approved by your father-in-law and mother-in-law. As the daughter of the Nanping Marquis’ household, if you can’t even tolerate this, you might as well leave now."

Hearing the faint sounds of drums and gongs from the front courtyard, Yu Qingci’s mind echoed the words her husband, Qiao Yuantao, had said to her a few days prior. She knew the new bride had already been welcomed in.

In the secluded back courtyard of the Qiao family, Yu Qingci sat motionless in a plain white dress before the vanity. The room was so silent one could hear a pin drop.

Everyone had gone to the front to join the festivities. Who would spare a thought for her, the legitimate wife, dying of illness?

She stared blankly at her reflection in the mirror—a face once youthful and tender, now weathered by time. Though only in her twenties, her complexion was pale and gaunt, her hollow, lifeless eyes filled only with deep loneliness and despair.

After a long while, she shifted her gaze to a small wooden box on the vanity. It was open, and inside, something was wrapped tightly in rice paper.

Footsteps approached the door, followed by a maid’s voice from behind: "Madam, are you done with your makeup? The guests have finished the banquet and left. Master, the new madam, the old master, the old mistress, the second young master, and the third young lady are all waiting for you in the front hall."

The maid spoke with no respect. She was bought by the old mistress and only listened to her, so she paid no mind to Yu Qingci, the mistress of the household.

Perhaps she had grown used to it. Yu Qingci showed no displeasure at the maid’s rudeness. She reached out, closed the small wooden box, and hugged it to her chest. With great effort, she stood up and turned slowly toward the door.

Her body had been deteriorating for the past two years. At first, she thought it was from overwork, but later she realized she had been poisoned with a slow-acting toxin. Death was near.

In an instant, her heart turned to ash.

The maid, seeing Yu Qingci in her plain white dress with only a single white jade hairpin, couldn’t help but frown. "Today is a joyous occasion with the new bride entering the household. Why is Madam dressed so plainly? When you reach the front hall, you’ll surely displease Master and the others."

Yu Qingci’s lips curled in a sarcastic smile. What did their displeasure matter? A house full of ingrates. If she still groveled and tried to please them as she had before, she would be a fool beyond saving.

Yu Qingci shuffled slowly toward the door.

The Qiao family’s courtyard was small, with only two sections. Even with her weak steps, she reached the front hall in the time it took to drink a cup of tea.

The moment Yu Qingci appeared, everyone in the front hall turned to look at her.

She saw her father-in-law and mother-in-law dressed in festive attire, seated in the center. To their left sat a young couple in bright red wedding garments—the man was her husband, Qiao Yuantao, looking proud and spirited. The woman beside him was adorned with jewels, her youthful and delicate face even more alluring in her wedding attire. It was her half-sister, Yu Lian.

To the right sat a young man and woman—her brother-in-law and sister-in-law.

Perfect. Since everyone who should be here was present, let the past be the past. Today, she would let it all vanish like smoke.

The moment she entered, the young sister-in-law’s eyes widened, and she jumped up, shouting, "Yu Qingci! On such a joyous day, why are you dressed like this? Are you doing this on purpose? Humph! You always act so virtuous, but now that my new sister-in-law has arrived, you deliberately dress like this. How wicked your intentions are!"

Old Mistress Qiao slammed the table in anger, her voice booming as usual: "Are you mourning someone? Anyone who doesn’t know better would think someone in the Qiao family has died! Tsk, tsk! Are you cursing us old folks into our coffins? You black-hearted, rotten thing! Hurry up and change, or get out!"

Qiao Yuantao’s radiant expression also darkened. He stood up and said to his wife, "Qingci, today I am taking Lian’er as a concubine with the approval of your father and mother. Are you trying to defy them? Besides, Lian’er has always respected you as her elder sister. Now that she has married into the family, you two should live in harmony. Your health has never been good, and you will need her care in the future. Since you’re here, come and meet Lian’er."

Yu Qingci’s icy gaze swept over him, then she lowered her eyes. She had no expectations left for this man. No matter how cold and heartless his words were, she didn’t want to respond.

Yu Lian, seeing her husband stand up, had intended to rise as well. But when she heard him ask her sister to come and meet her, she felt a surge of pride. She remained seated and said to Yu Qingci:

"Elder sister, do you resent Master for marrying me? Sister has been married to Master for ten years and yet couldn’t even bear a single child. Mother only arranged for me to marry in to restore the reputation of the Marquis’ daughters and to ensure Master has an heir."

As she spoke, she glanced shyly at Qiao Yuantao, then lowered her head and gently rubbed her stomach. Now that she was married, there was no need to hide her pregnancy any longer.

The "mother" Yu Lian referred to was not Yu Qingci’s birth mother, but her father’s other wife, Qiao née Qiao.

Yu Qingci’s heart filled with even more hatred. In her ten years of marriage to the Qiao family, she had been pregnant before. During her first pregnancy, her mother-in-law had kept her by her side to teach her the rules of the household. The exhaustion had caused her to miscarry at three months, and she had been blamed by her mother-in-law for being careless and unable to carry a child.

Later, she became pregnant again. At five months, she was pushed by her spoiled sister-in-law and miscarried once more. The Qiao family, to cover up the incident, had not even called a doctor.

That time, she had nearly lost her life, and from then on, her body was ruined, leaving her unable to bear children ever again.

Yu Qingci listened to their accusations with a blank expression. She looked around at everyone in the room, a mocking smile appearing on her lips.

"Today is my sister’s joyous day. Didn’t my husband always urge me to give her a generous gift? I’ve brought one."

With that, she raised the wooden box in her hand. Everyone in the room looked over, their eyes filled with greed.

Old Mistress Qiao’s expression shifted from anger to pleasure. She coldly huffed, "At least you know better. Lian’er, go and accept it."

Yu Lian couldn’t wait for her mother-in-law’s command. She stood up and walked toward Yu Qingci.

Yu Qingci’s heart filled with cold laughter. When she had first married into the Qiao family, her father had still cared for her as his daughter. Her mother, Su, had also given her most of her personal savings, so her dowry had been quite substantial.

The Qiao family, however, was merely a branch of the Qiao Minister’s household, with little to their name besides this small two-section courtyard. Over the years, her in-laws had always coveted her dowry.

On the second day after her marriage, her mother-in-law had found an excuse to take over the household finances. In her desire to maintain a virtuous reputation, she had foolishly used her dowry to support the entire family for ten years. Now, all she had left was this broken body.

Yu Lian approached, giving Yu Qingci a charming smile. She swayed her waist deliberately, revealing a palm-sized jade pendant tied around it.

The jade was warm in color and exquisitely carved. Yu Qingci recognized it immediately—it had been left to her by her mother. A few years ago, her husband had taken it from her, saying he would return it after a while. She had never gotten it back, and now she saw it hanging from Yu Lian’s waist.

So they had been in cahoots for years.

Yu Lian, seeing her staring intently at the jade pendant, smiled triumphantly. "Does this jade pendant look familiar, sister? It was a token of love Master specially gave to me. Even though I know it was your beloved treasure, I can’t bear to part with it. You won’t be angry with me, will you?"

Seeing Yu Qingci’s face turn ashen, Yu Lian grew even more pleased. She took a step closer and said, "Speaking of which, you were just lucky to be registered under Mother’s name. Your late birth mother was nothing but a concubine. So, deep down, you’re also a bastard. Don’t put on airs as a legitimate elder sister in front of me."

---

chapters.title: Reborn and Returned
chapters.content:
These provocative words, however, did not anger Yu Qingci. She withdrew her gaze, a strange smile flashing across her lips. She lowered her head and slowly opened the wooden box in her hands. Her icy voice rang out again:

"It’s just a piece of jade. Of course, I won’t be angry. I thought the firecrackers outside weren’t lively enough, so I decided to add a little more celebration."

With that, she pulled the fuse with one hand, her challenging gaze sweeping over everyone in the room. The people in the room were all stunned by her strange expression and actions.

Yu Lian instinctively took a step back. "What is this?"

Yu Qingci’s smile grew even stranger. "It’s—gunpowder."

Yu Lian’s eyes widened in shock. "Gun... gunpowder? What do you mean, sister?"

Yu Qingci took a step forward, pressing closer. "Since you all want my life so badly, let’s none of us live."

She had prepared this package of gunpowder ever since she learned they wanted her dead. Now, it would finally serve its purpose.

When Qiao Yuantao heard the word "gunpowder," a terrible premonition surged through him. He abruptly stood up from his chair, reaching out to stop her.

"What are you doing? Qingci, calm down! Don’t do anything stupid!"

The people in the room finally realized what was happening, and their expressions changed.

The two elders of the Qiao family panicked and scrambled to their feet, trying to flee. The young sister-in-law began cursing loudly.

Seeing the panic on everyone’s faces, the smile on Yu Qingci’s face became even more chilling.

Just as Qiao Yuantao was about to reach her and snatch the object from her hands, Yu Qingci pulled the fuse with all her strength.

A deafening *bang* echoed through the air!

In an instant, the front hall of the Qiao household was engulfed in flames. A series of tragic screams filled the air, lingering for a long time.

Soon, the entire courtyard was consumed by fire...

Yu Qingci regained consciousness and found herself lying on an exceptionally soft bed.

Looking at the goose-yellow canopy embroidered with intricate flowers above her, and then at the furnishings in the room, everything was eerily familiar.

This was the residence her family had lived in when they first returned to the capital from Youyang, over ten years ago!

It seemed she had experienced a very long dream. In the dream, she had lived through a future life—shortly after returning to the capital, she married, endured immense hardship in her marital home, and ultimately met a tragic end, perishing alongside her in-laws.

Was this what people called a "Yellow Millet Dream"?

But she hadn’t drunk any Yellow Millet wine. Even if it was a dream, it felt too real—real as if she had lived through it herself, real enough to send chills down her spine.

Her father was a nobleman of the capital, the Marquis of Nanping. But this residence was not the Marquis’ mansion; it was the old Su family home, her mother’s maiden family. This time, when her father was transferred back to the capital, their family had followed him.

This boudoir had been specially arranged for her by her mother. Unfortunately, they had only lived here for a few days before her father took her, her mother, and her younger brother back to the Marquis’ mansion.

The little maid, Tong’er, saw that she was awake and quickly approached, carefully wiping the sweat from her forehead with a warm, damp cloth. She muttered worriedly, "Young lady, you’re awake. You didn’t sleep well last night. How are you feeling now? Would you like something to eat?"

Yu Qingci looked at Tong’er’s small, delicate face. Tong’er was still alive. They were all still alive?!

Tong’er, seeing her eyes redden, thought she was unwell and hurriedly asked, "Are you feeling unwell, young lady? Don’t worry, this servant will go report to the Marquis and the mistress."

Before she could finish, footsteps were heard outside, followed by a childish voice: "Sister, we’ve come to see you."

Yu Qingci looked over and saw her father, mother, and younger brother, Qingbai, had already reached her bedside.

Seeing the familiar faces before her, Yu Qingci’s heart ached sharply once more, bringing tears to her eyes.

Su Cheng, her mother, quickly stepped forward, pulling her daughter into her arms and placing a hand on her forehead to check her temperature.

Yu Qingci looked up at her mother’s still youthful, gentle, and beautifully refined face, so close to her. It was not the emaciated, wretched woman from her dream. She barely suppressed the bitterness in her heart and, after a long moment, lifted her head and said:

"I’m much better. I’ve caused you and Father worry; your daughter is unfilial."

Her father, Yu Jingcheng, also approached with concern. "Perhaps the long journey wore you out. Now that we’ve arrived in the capital, I’ll have the Marquis’ physician come examine you."

Yu Qingci’s gaze fell on her father, her heart filled with a mix of emotions. Her father, though shrewd and decisive in his official career and highly regarded by the court, was often muddle-headed in his personal life, easily swayed by what he saw before him.

In her past life, after returning to the Marquis’ mansion, Qiao Shi had schemed repeatedly, driving a wedge between her father and mother. Eventually, she, her mother, and her brother had been outmaneuvered and met a tragic end.

Now, seeing the father who had disappointed her so thoroughly in her past life, Yu Qingci clenched her fists secretly.

In this life, she must not easily turn against her father. She needed to firmly grasp this powerful backer to protect herself, her mother, and her brother.

Yu Qingci shook her head. "Thank you, Father. I just had a nightmare last night and didn’t sleep well. Now I’ve slept enough and feel much better. There’s really no need for a physician."

Yu Jingcheng carefully observed her complexion and, satisfied that she was fine, let out a sigh of relief. "That’s good. I’ve already sent word to the Marquis’ mansion. Originally, I planned to take you back today, but since you’re unwell, we’ll rest here for another day and return tomorrow."

Yu Qingci’s hand, hidden in her sleeve, tightened abruptly at the mention of returning to the Marquis’ mansion. In her past life, all the tragedies had begun when she and her mother and brother followed her father back to the Marquis’ mansion.

Sure enough, she heard her father say to her mother, "Cheng, I’ll go to the Marquis’ mansion to see my mother today. I won’t be back tonight. I’ll come for you all early tomorrow morning."

Yu Qingci noticed her mother’s arms, which were wrapped around her, tighten slightly. It seemed that from the very beginning, her mother had been reluctant to return to the Marquis’ mansion with her father.

Her mother was her father’s original, legitimate wife. Over a decade ago, her maternal grandfather’s family, who had been officials in the capital, had fallen from grace, and the entire family was imprisoned. The old mistress of the Marquis’ mansion, her paternal grandmother, had taken the opportunity to try to demote her mother to the status of a concubine, so her son could marry the daughter-in-law she truly desired.

At that time, her father had been away from the capital. Her mother, left alone and helpless, had been forced to expose herself to public view, day and night seeking help for her imprisoned family, but to no avail. In the end, when the case against her maternal grandfather’s family was decided, her grandfather and grandmother were sentenced to exile.

Her mother, strong-willed by nature, had been so grieved and indignant that she had confronted her grandmother, declaring she would rather be divorced than become a concubine. With a letter of divorce in hand, she had left the Marquis’ mansion to follow her exiled parents.

Meanwhile, her grandmother had quickly arranged for her father to marry Qiao Shi, the legitimate daughter of the Qiao Minister’s household, shortly after her mother’s departure.

By the time her father had returned to the capital after completing his duties, everything had been settled. Her grandmother had already welcomed the new bride, Qiao Shi, into the family.

Fortunately, her father had always cared for her mother and had continued to search for her. Years later, he had reunited with her mother in Youyang, thousands of miles away.

At that time, her father, then the heir of the Marquis’ mansion, had already had a promising career in the capital. But for her mother’s sake, he had resigned from his position in the capital and requested a post in Youyang, where he had served for over a decade.

So, as far back as she could remember, she knew that her grandmother in the distant capital despised her mother, and by extension, disowned her and her brother as well.

chapters.title: Mother is the Legitimate Wife
chapters.content:
In her dream, for the sake of her and her brother’s recognition by the family, her mother had returned to the Marquis of Nanping’s estate as a concubine. In the end, none of the three of them had a good fate.

And the first one to be schemed against was her.

In the dream, they didn’t know that the reason Grandmother had agreed to let their father take them back to be recognized by the family was to have her take the place of Yu Qingyan, the daughter born to Lady Qiao, in marriage.

But this marriage was to a widower of the Shuangwang Gate.

Yu Qingyan had been betrothed since childhood to a man who died in battle. Lady Qiao was unwilling for her daughter to marry into a family as a widow, so she schemed to have her take Yu Qingyan’s place. When her mother found out the truth, she firmly refused this marriage, even going so far as to defy Grandmother and cause a scene in the inner quarters.

In the end, her mother protected her, and Yu Qingyan had no choice but to marry into the family, carrying her late husband’s spirit tablet.

Lady Qiao held this grudge against them, and to take revenge, she schemed to have her involved with Qiao Yuantao, the son of her maternal uncle, forcing her to marry him.

At that time, Qiao Yuantao’s branch of the family had already split from the Qiao Minister’s estate, Lady Qiao’s maiden home, and could only be considered a collateral branch of the Qiao family.

That family had always fawned over Lady Qiao, who had married into a noble family. After Qiao Yuantao successfully married her under Lady Qiao’s scheme, he became even more obedient to his aunt.

He knew that Lady Qiao despised Yu Qingci and her mother, wishing to eliminate them. To please Lady Qiao, after marriage, he was always cold and harsh to Yu Qingci, and the rest of his family followed suit. Thus, Yu Qingci never had a single good day in her married home.

Soon, Lady Qiao helped Qiao Yuantao secure a position in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. A few years later, he became a seventh-rank official in charge of records, officially gaining an official status.

Yu Qingci had not known any of this at first. Naively, she thought she must have done something wrong to displease her husband and in-laws. So, she willingly took on the household duties, using her dowry to support the entire family.

She thought that as long as she was filial to her parents-in-law, considerate to her husband, and kind to her brothers- and sisters-in-law, they would eventually see her goodness.

In the end, they joined forces to take her life.

Heaven took pity on her, allowing her to reincarnate. Fortunately, they had not yet returned to the Marquis’s estate, and she had not yet married into that family.

Regardless of whether everything in the dream had truly happened, she was grateful that she had awakened at the last moment of her life, taking revenge on those who had wronged her.

Now that Heaven had given her a second chance, before any of this happened, she must prepare and stop it all.

The first thing she needed to do was stop her mother from returning to the Marquis’s estate.

After sorting through these thoughts, Yu Qingci lifted her head and asked, "Mother, do we really have to return to the Marquis’s estate?"

Su Chengniang frowned at the question, and Yu Jingcheng also looked at his daughter in surprise. "Of course we have to return. Otherwise, why would I bring you all the way back to the capital?"

Yu Qingci knitted her brows. "But under what status will Mother return?"

Yu Jingcheng looked at his daughter in bewilderment. He hadn’t expected her to ask this so suddenly. After a moment, he still replied, "Your mother is my lawful wife. When we return, she will naturally still be my lawful wife."

But his tone lacked confidence.

Yu Qingci pressed further, "Then what about the lady at the estate? Surely Father can’t have two wives. There must be a distinction between primary and secondary."

Su Chengniang also turned to look at him, her gaze cold, but she remained silent.

She was indeed his lawful wife. But in the capital, the mistress of the Marquis of Nanping’s estate had long been Lady Qiao, not her, Su Chengniang.

The divorce letter she had received years ago was not written by Yu Jingcheng himself but by the old lady of the Marquis’s estate. It didn’t bear her husband’s signature, so according to the laws of the current dynasty, it shouldn’t have been valid.

However, after she left the estate, the old lady had spread the news far and wide, making it known throughout the capital that Su Chengniang had been divorced by the Marquis’s estate.

Soon after, the estate had grandly married Yu Jingcheng to a new wife, Lady Qiao. So, in the eyes of the world, the mistress of the Marquis of Nanping’s estate was now Lady Qiao.

Yu Jingcheng was also troubled. Before deciding to return with his family, he had mentioned Su Chengniang’s status to his mother in letters, but his mother had never agreed, only willing to give Su Chengniang the position of a concubine.

He didn’t dare to tell Su Chengniang this directly. Since his daughter was still young, he didn’t want her to know about these inner family conflicts. So, when discussing the return to the capital with them, he had avoided this topic. He hadn’t expected his daughter to bring it up now.

Yu Jingcheng looked at Su Chengniang and said, "Chengniang, I know you’ve always been resentful about what happened back then. But in my heart, I only recognize you as my lawful wife. I’ve told my mother that the divorce letter from back then wasn’t written by me, and since it didn’t have my signature, it shouldn’t count.

Rest assured, once we return to the estate, I won’t let you and the children suffer."

But Su Chengniang just gave a cold laugh after listening. "My lord has thought of everything. But apart from you, I’m afraid no one in the Marquis’s estate will acknowledge me as the lawful wife."

Yu Jingcheng’s face showed an embarrassed expression. Yu Qingci silently watched, knowing that at this moment, her father did care about her mother and siblings. However, the promises he had just made might not be kept.

Her father was the Marquis of Nanping and held an official position. He couldn’t stay in the inner quarters all day watching over them. In places where her father couldn’t see, it would be easy for Grandmother and Lady Qiao to make life difficult for them.

In her dream, not long after her mother entered the Marquis’s estate, to prevent her from replacing Yu Qingyan in marriage to the Shuangwang Gate as a widow, her mother had defied Grandmother, thoroughly offending her. With Lady Qiao also targeting her from the side, her mother’s life in the inner quarters had been extremely difficult.

Lady Qiao took the opportunity to secretly scheme, repeatedly provoking and framing her mother, which gradually turned her father against her mother.

Later, Lady Qiao framed her mother for adultery, causing her father to completely despise her mother. In just a few years, her mother was tormented to the point of emaciation and soon passed away.

Seeing her father’s embarrassed expression, Yu Qingci spoke up, "Not to mention that Mother’s status is unclear now, we’ve also brought back the spirit tablets of Grandfather and Grandmother. Mother is their only daughter and is in deep mourning. If we return to the Marquis’s estate at this time, won’t Grandmother be even more displeased?"

Yu Jingcheng quickly said, "Why would she be displeased? This time, it was your grandmother who personally agreed to let you return. She even wants to open the ancestral hall for you and Qingbai to be recognized by the family. As for your mother’s mourning, once we’re in the Marquis’s estate, she can observe it in her own courtyard."

After saying this, he looked at Su Chengniang to reassure her, "Chengniang, rest assured. The Marquis’s estate has already prepared a place for you and the children. Once we return, you won’t have to worry about the estate’s affairs. You can just stay in your own courtyard and focus on your mourning. You can do whatever you want."

Yu Qingci pretended to be naive and asked again, "Father once said that the Marquis’s estate is a noble family with strict rules. Would Grandmother allow Mother to burn paper money and offer sacrifices to Grandfather and Grandmother in her own courtyard?"

---

chapters.title: Not Returning to the Marquis’s Estate
chapters.content:
Yu Jingcheng was momentarily speechless. Su Chengniang looked at him and gave another cold laugh. She had already suspected that her husband was hiding something when he told her about these matters. To get her and the children to return to the capital with him, who knew what conditions he had agreed to with the old lady.

Thinking of this, she couldn’t help but coldly scoff, "My lord, how do you know the old lady won’t mind a person in deep mourning living in the estate? If we hide this from her and she finds out from somewhere else later, won’t I have another crime to bear?"

Yu Qingci looked at her father and said, "It’s not Grandmother’s fault for being displeased. Which family would want someone to keep spirit tablets and burn paper money in their backyard? Grandmother already has a bias against Mother. If this matter angers her further, it would be a loss. Therefore, I think now is absolutely not a good time for Mother to enter the Marquis’s estate."

After saying this, she looked around and continued, "Why don’t we just not return? My brother and I can stay with Mother at Grandfather’s home. Anyway, the Su residence is empty now, and we can do whatever we want while living here."

Mother was the only child of Grandfather and Grandmother, so the Su residence had been empty before they returned.

Yu Jingcheng hadn’t expected his usually obedient daughter to oppose him at this moment. He couldn’t help but darken his face and say, "Don’t be willful. Since we’ve returned to the capital, how can we live outside and not go home?"

Yu Qingci looked at her mother, her voice soft and sweet, "But I truly don’t want to see Mother suffer in the Marquis’s estate."

Su Chengniang hadn’t expected her daughter to consider her so much. She couldn’t help but embrace her daughter tightly with a look of pity. "Alright, I’ll listen to my daughter. We won’t return to the Marquis’s estate. We’ll live at the Su residence."

Beside them, Yu Qingbai also chimed in with a clear voice, "Then I won’t go back either. Wherever Mother and Sister go, I’ll go too."

Looking at the affectionate scene of the mother and children, Yu Jingcheng helplessly said, "Chengniang, how can you be so confused? You’ve finally returned to the capital with me. The estate has already prepared to open the ancestral hall and register the children in the family genealogy. Didn’t you also agree to return to the capital for the sake of giving the children a proper status?"

Su Chengniang hesitated again when he mentioned the children. Over the years, because the old lady had disliked her, she had refused to acknowledge her two children and even prevented her son from including them in the family genealogy. The reason she had agreed to return to the capital this time was to give her children a legitimate status so they could stand proudly in front of others.

Yu Qingci knew that her mother was willing to endure hardship for the sake of her and her brother. She quickly said, "If that’s the case, then only my brother and I will follow Father back to the estate to be recognized by the family. Mother can stay here to properly mourn Grandfather and Grandmother. After the mourning period is over, she can return to the estate. This way, nothing will be delayed.

Moreover, Grandfather was finally exonerated last year. The Su family has no other relatives left in the capital except for Mother, my brother, and me. Mother staying at the Su residence for a year or so to pray for Grandfather and Grandmother’s spirits in heaven would also be a way for our family to fulfill our filial duties. After all, this is Grandfather’s home, so it would be convenient for Mother to do whatever she needs here.

Mother doesn’t need to worry about my brother and me. After all, we are Father’s legitimate children. Even if Grandmother doesn’t like us, she won’t make things difficult for us. Besides, I’m already fifteen years old and won’t be able to stay at the Marquis’s estate for much longer.

As for my brother, there’s even less to worry about. He’s a grandson, so Grandmother will naturally dote on him. Moreover, my brother is already nine years old by traditional reckoning. After returning, he’ll live in the outer courtyard and have Father looking after him. He’ll also be attending school every day, so he won’t actually spend much time at the Marquis’s estate.

If Mother misses us, she can ask Father to bring my brother and me to visit her often."

Yu Qingci was determined to prevent her mother from returning to the Marquis’s estate and persuaded her with well-reasoned arguments.

Su Chengniang had always been reluctant to return to the Marquis’s estate. Now, under her daughter’s persuasion, she finally made up her mind. "We’ll do as my daughter says. I’ll stay at the Su residence to mourn my parents for a year. You can take the children back with you."

Yu Qingci secretly breathed a sigh of relief. As long as her mother was convinced, her father would have no choice. As for what would happen after a year, they would cross that bridge when they came to it.

Yu Jingcheng sighed helplessly once more. "What Chengniang says makes sense, but how do we explain this to the Marquis’s estate?"

Su Chengniang coldly laughed. "My lord, rest assured. If I don’t return to the Marquis’s estate, the old lady might be even more pleased. Perhaps she’ll even praise me for being sensible."

She still remembered the old lady of the Marquis of Nanping’s exact words from ten years ago: *How could the daughter of a criminal possibly be worthy of being the mistress of our Marquis of Nanping’s estate? It’s simply a joke! The fact that we didn’t divorce you already shows our estate’s great tolerance. Even as a concubine or a mistress, our Marquis of Nanping’s estate only accepts daughters from clean and respectable families. And you, Su Chengniang, are not worthy!*

---

At the Marquis of Nanping’s estate, in the Shouyin Hall, the residence of the old lady.

Old Lady Zhang abruptly slammed her prayer beads heavily on the table. "Nonsense! If the people have been brought back, they should be brought directly to the estate. Why are they being settled outside? Do you want the entire capital to know that you’ve kept a mistress outside?"

Yu Jingcheng said, "Mother, please calm down. How can Chengniang be a mistress? Back then, she was my lawfully wedded wife. If it weren’t for—"

"Enough with the nonsense!" Old Lady Zhang furiously interrupted. "Your wife is Lady Qiao. How could a daughter of a criminal like that Su woman be worthy of being the mistress of our Marquis of Nanping’s estate?"

Yu Jingcheng, recalling the past, felt helpless. But the person in front of him was his mother, so he could only try to soothe her. "Mother, please be careful with your words. My father-in-law was exonerated last year. You mustn’t say such things anymore."

Old Lady Zhang was relentless. "Who is your father-in-law? You’d better recognize this clearly. Your current father-in-law is Lord Qiao of the Minister’s estate, a second-rank official in the imperial court, not that incompetent man who died in a foreign land.

Even if the Su family has been exonerated, what does it matter? Even if they were wronged back then, the fact remains that Su Chengniang was never destined to be a lawful wife!"

Yu Jingcheng’s tone couldn’t help but carry a hint of resentment. "If Mother hadn’t taken it upon herself to drive Chengniang out of the estate while I was away from the capital, she and the children would have been safely at the estate all these years. None of this would have happened."

Old Lady Zhang retorted, "Are you blaming me, your mother, for breaking up your marriage? Back then, it wasn’t our family who caused trouble for her family. They had offended a nobleman, and which family wouldn’t fear being implicated in such a life-threatening matter? In any other family, she would have been divorced outright.

At that time, I had already shown her enough mercy by only making her leave the estate. I even allowed her to stay as a concubine, but it was she, Su Chengniang, who was too proud to bow her head. Whose fault is that?"

Hmph! Back then, she had said she would never be a concubine. Now, if she wants to return, she must accept the status of a concubine and kneel before me to admit her mistakes.

Recalling how Su Chengniang had knelt before her in humiliation, Old Lady Zhang felt a surge of satisfaction.

Just wait until she enters the estate. I’ll show her what happens then!

chapters.title: The Inner Residence of the Bo Mansion
chapters.content:
Yu Jingcheng straightforwardly said, "Let them, mother and children, stay at the Su residence for now. In a few days, I will bring Qingci and Qingbai, the two children, back to the mansion. They are your own grandchildren, and I hope you will take good care of them in the future. As for Chengniang—"

Madame Zhang's eyes turned cold. "What? If you want to elevate Su to a higher status, you'd better shut your mouth. I haven't settled the score with her yet. For such a vixen, it's already more than generous of me to allow her back with the status of a lowly concubine. Don't even think about anything else—she doesn't deserve it!

And what's wrong with your current wife, Qiao? Since your father passed away, my health has been poor, and hasn't the entire mansion been managed by your wife? But you—over these years, your heart has only been with that Su woman. For her, you were willing to go to a poor, remote place like Youyang and stay there for over a decade. How can you face Qiao and me, your old mother?"

If it weren't for the fact that the Su family's case had been overturned and the two elders had met with misfortune and died abroad, she would never have agreed to let her son bring that mother and her children back.

Yu Jingcheng helplessly reminded her, "Mother, the divorce letter back then didn't have my signature, so it was invalid. Therefore, Chengniang's status is still my lawful wife.

As for Qiao, considering her years of companionship and dedication to the Bo mansion, I won't treat her unfairly. I will give her the status of a secondary wife. In the future, the management of the household affairs will still be her responsibility. That's settled."

Before Madame Zhang could speak, Yu Jingcheng continued, "Chengniang is currently in mourning. It would be inappropriate for her to return to the mansion at this time. Since her father has only her as a daughter, this time I will only bring the two children back. As for Chengniang, she will stay at the Su family's old residence in Liuli Alley. After her mourning period is over, we can bring her back to the mansion."

Madame Zhang became even more furious upon hearing this. "So you've already arranged everything? You're always protecting that wretched Su woman, and now you're even letting her live outside, free and happy?"

Yu Jingcheng: "It's just a temporary measure. After all, she is in mourning, and it would be inauspicious for her to enter the mansion now. If Mother disagrees, should I bring her back immediately?"

Madame Zhang was so angry she could die. What was the point of bringing her back?

It seemed that no matter what she said, her son had already made up his mind to elevate Su. Now he even wanted that wretched woman to stay outside and not return. Fine, fine, he was truly her good son.

Unable to help herself, she raised her voice again, "Everyone in the capital knew that Su had been divorced. Now you want to restore her status as your lawful wife? Don't even think about it! I won't agree, and your current father-in-law won't agree either. Since she wants to mourn outside, let her stay out there forever and never return!"

Yu Jingcheng's face darkened, and he fell silent. The room was quiet for a while. Seeing that her son wasn't speaking, Madame Zhang began to regret speaking so absolutely.

She secretly pondered that her son's words weren't without reason. Bringing someone in mourning back into the mansion would indeed be inauspicious. It would be better to let her stay outside and finish her mourning period before returning.

Then she could deal with her properly!

After figuring this out, Madame Zhang let out a heavy humph through her nose and said, "As for those two children, after they enter the mansion, we'll see if they're worthy of my affection.

They grew up with that untamed mother of theirs and certainly don't understand the rules and etiquette of a noble family. After they enter the mansion, they'll need to be retaught. I've already discussed this with your wife. Later, have her hire a special governess to properly educate these two children."

Mentioning the sister and brother who would soon enter the mansion, Madame Zhang's anger slightly subsided. After all, they were her own grandchildren whom she had never met, so she had to give them some face.

"This matter has indeed wronged your wife. Later, when you see her, say some kind words to her. You've been away from the mansion for years, and all the big and small matters of the mansion have been managed by her hard work."

Yu Jingcheng immediately stood up and respectfully bowed upon hearing this. "Yes, I will remember."

At this moment, Madame Qiao of the South Ping Bo family was in her Haitang Courtyard with her daughter, sorting through accounts. After listening to the report from her close maid, Zhishu, she couldn't help but be surprised. "What? The Master actually wants to place Su outside?"

Zhishu nodded. "Yes, I heard it directly from Sister Xichun, who serves the Old Madame. The Master also told the Old Madame that tomorrow he would only bring the sister and brother back to acknowledge their ancestors and clan. As for that woman, I heard that because she is in mourning, the Old Madame won't allow her to enter the mansion."

Madame Qiao frowned. "In mourning? Who passed away?"

Zhishu: "I heard it was her parents."

After clarifying, Madame Qiao let out a cold laugh. This Su Chengniang truly wasn't favored by heaven. Back then, her maternal family had been disgraced, and she was divorced by the Bo family. Now, just as her maternal family's case was overturned, her parents had died in a foreign land. What terrible luck!

But if Su didn't enter the mansion, how would she carry out her many plans?

Zhishu stammered, "I also heard, I heard that..."

Madame Qiao looked at her suspiciously. "What else did you hear? Just say it."

Zhishu leaned close to Madame Qiao's ear and whispered a few words.

Madame Qiao was furious and slammed her hand hard on the nearby tea table.

"So there is such a thing. Did you find out for sure?"

Zhishu nodded vigorously. "I wouldn't dare lie. Sister Xichun told me exactly that."

Madame Qiao was so angry that she swept a set of fine celadon teacups off the table. Zhishu was so scared that she knelt on the ground.

Yu Qingyan, the eldest daughter, couldn't sit still any longer. She grabbed Madame Qiao's hand. "Mother, wasn't Su already divorced? How can Father restore her status as his lawful wife? Could Father be planning to divorce you for her?"

Madame Qiao hatefully said, "He'd better not think about it! Not to mention your maternal grandfather won't agree, even the Old Madame won't allow that wretched Su to return as the mistress of the Bo mansion."

She hadn't expected that after so many years, the Master would heartlessly abandon the entire Bo mansion to be with Su in a remote place for over a decade. The Bo mansion, up and down, had relied on her hard work to manage, and now the Master actually wanted to demote her to a secondary wife for that Su woman. It was simply outrageous!

The inside story of the divorce letter was unknown to others, but Madame Qiao had long since found out. If it really came down to it, in terms of status, that Su woman still held the position of lawful wife, and the Master was deeply in love with her. So if Su returned, she would pose the greatest threat to Madame Qiao's position.

She would never allow such a thing to happen.

After calming her anger for a while, she looked at her daughter and softly said, "Don't worry, Mother will never let this happen. Your position as the eldest legitimate daughter will never be shaken. It's good that Su isn't returning to the mansion; it will make it easier for us to plan slowly."

In this dynasty, although children born to a secondary wife were also considered legitimate, they were still inferior to the children of the lawful wife. So for the sake of her own children, she couldn't allow her position as the lawful wife to be shaken.

Yu Qingyan was somewhat reassured by her mother's comforting words. Over the years, her father had been away from home constantly, and the entire Bo mansion had been managed by her mother. Even if her father wanted to change her mother's position as the lawful wife, her grandmother certainly wouldn't agree.

---

chapters.title: Widow Before the Door
chapters.content:
Ever since she could remember, she knew how much her grandmother despised the woman outside who had ensnared her father and kept him from coming home, along with her children. If they thought they could climb above her, they were dreaming.

Yu Qingyan frowned and asked, "Mother, if Su doesn't return to the mansion, will the matter you promised me change?"

In recent days, people from the Ningyuan General's mansion had been repeatedly urging them, and now even the wedding date had been set. Her mother had said that she would find a way to have Su's daughter marry in her place. So upon hearing this news, Yu Qingyan was more anxious than anyone else.

This deadly marriage loomed over her like a huge boulder, making her restless day and night. She was only sixteen years old; her life had just begun. How could she be expected to spend the rest of her life as a widow in the Ningyuan General's mansion, tending to a memorial tablet?

Madame Qiao saw her daughter's anxious and flustered appearance and came back to her senses. She softly comforted her, "Good child, didn't Zhishu just say that your father will bring that sister and brother back to the mansion to acknowledge their family in a few days? As long as that little wretch, Yu Qingci, returns to the mansion, Mother will find a way to have her marry in your place. Don't worry; Mother will never let you marry over there."

Only then did Yu Qingyan feel at ease.

Madame Qiao continued, "Later, when your father comes, be understanding and considerate, and try to win his favor. Remember, don't show any unwillingness about this marriage in front of your father. It would be best if you could make him feel guilty toward you, his daughter. That would be more advantageous for us."

Yu Qingyan looked at her mother trustingly and nodded.

Madame Qiao affectionately caressed her daughter's delicate, well-maintained face. This was her precious daughter, whom she had raised with the utmost care in the wealthy and noble South Ping Bo mansion. In terms of appearance, talents, etiquette, and demeanor, she was no worse than any other noble lady in the capital. In fact, she was a shining pearl among them.

She had hoped that her daughter would marry into a good family and bring more support to the South Ping Bo mansion. How could she be forced to marry into the General's mansion to be a widow tending to a memorial tablet?

Yu Jingcheng returned to the Haitang Courtyard where he and his wife lived. Madame Qiao and her daughter, Yu Qingyan, hurriedly came forward to attend to him. Madame Qiao personally served Yu Jingcheng as he washed and changed clothes. After a flurry of activity, they finally sat down.

Yu Qingyan poured a cup of freshly brewed Tieguanyin tea and placed it in front of Yu Jingcheng. With a respectful expression, she said, "Father, you must be tired from your long journey. This is the tea I personally brewed for you. Please try it, Father."

Yu Jingcheng hummed in acknowledgment and took the teacup. As he lifted the lid, a sweet and refreshing tea aroma wafted out, instantly making him feel refreshed in body and mind.

Yu Jingcheng saw the look of dependence and admiration on his daughter's face. He couldn't help but think of how he had been away for so many years and had paid little attention to this daughter. So he smiled and praised her a few words before lowering his head to sip the tea.

Yu Qingyan sat down on a chair on the other side of her father. Her voice was gentle and pleasant as she said, "Father, you have been working away from home for years, and I have always been worried about you. Now that you have finally been transferred back to the capital to reunite with us, I am truly overjoyed. From now on, I can be by your side every day, listening to your teachings."

Yu Jingcheng put down the teacup and looked at his daughter seriously. Of course, he cared about this daughter. He had indeed neglected his children at home over the years due to his constant absence. Now, hearing his daughter say this, he couldn't help but feel a pang of guilt. Thinking about how this child had the misfortune to be saddled with such a troublesome marriage, his guilt deepened.

He couldn't help but sigh softly, "Qingyan, you've grown up. You're becoming more and more considerate and filial. As your father, I am truly gratified."

Madame Qiao also looked at her daughter with a loving expression. "Qingyan is the eldest legitimate daughter. Since she was a child, she has been obedient, considerate, and filial to her elders. As for the rules and etiquette that a young lady should learn, there's no need to mention—she's mastered them all. That's why, among so many grandchildren, I love our Qingyan the most."

Seeing her mother praising her, Yu Qingyan shyly lowered her head.

The three of them chatted harmoniously for a while before Yu Qingyan stood up and said, "Father, you must be exhausted from your journey. I won't disturb your rest any longer. I'll take my leave now."

Watching her daughter's retreating figure, Madame Qiao's face was filled with sorrow as she sighed, "Such a good daughter. I've done everything in my power to raise her. Since she was a child, she's studied music, chess, calligraphy, painting, household management, etiquette, and rules. I've made her into a shining pearl who is in no way inferior to any noble lady in the capital. Who doesn't praise her when they see her?

I never expected that fate would be so cruel. Now, she's being forced to marry into the General's mansion to be a widow tending to a memorial tablet. These past few days, every time I see Qingyan, my heart aches unbearably."

With that, Madame Qiao covered her mouth with a handkerchief and silently wept. Yu Jingcheng also felt a deep sorrow.

It was indeed a cruel twist of fate. This marriage had been personally arranged by the old Marquis of Bo when he was alive, with Ningyuan Grand General. The Grand General and his son were both military officers who had spent years fighting on the frontier and had achieved great merits for the court.

The one betrothed to the Bo family was the Grand General's only legitimate son, Lu Yunqi, a young and talented man known as the Young General.

Back then, the old Marquis and the Old Madame had taken a fancy to this son-in-law at first sight and had only been waiting for Qingyan to come of age to marry him.

A few months ago, news of a great victory from the border arrived, but it also brought terrible news: the Ningyuan Grand General and the Young General, father and son, had both died in battle.

What was even more heartbreaking was that only the Grand General's body had been returned with the army. As for the Young General, it was said that not even his body could be found.

Now, the main branch of the General's mansion was left with only a widow and a young girl who had not yet come of age. From then on, there would be no one to carry on the family line, truly leaving them as orphans and a widow. This turn of events had left the world sighing in sympathy.

After the funerals of the two generals, the General's mansion sent someone to deliver a message, hoping that the South Ping Bo mansion would honor the marriage agreement and send their daughter over to support the family. In the future, they could adopt a child from the clan to continue the Young General's lineage.

These days, everyone in the capital had been discussing this matter, all sympathizing with the two generals who had died for their country.

Public opinion always favored the weak. Facing the General's mansion, which now had only a widow and a weak young girl who had lost their father and brother, many people believed that the South Ping Bo mansion should honor their promise and send their daughter over to comfort the spirits of the two generals in heaven.

Even the current Emperor had mentioned this matter during a morning court session, implying that the South Ping Bo mansion, being a family of loyal officials for generations, would naturally not do something as dishonorable as breaking their promise and leaving the General's mansion without an heir.

Since the Emperor had expressed himself in this way, it was as if he had personally decreed the completion of this marriage, putting the South Ping Bo mansion in a very difficult position.

There was no other way but to send their daughter over to demonstrate that the South Ping Bo mansion was not a family that broke promises.

Yu Jingcheng sighed deeply and tried to console Madame Qiao, "Things have come to this. Don't be too sad. Try to look on the bright side. I've heard that the Old Madame of the General's mansion is very kind, with a gentle temper and a generous nature. The young girl she has raised also has the demeanor of a noble lady. After Qingyan marries over there, she will be the mistress of the General's mansion. As long as she fulfills her duties, respects her mother-in-law, and takes care of her sister-in-law, and then adopts a child, with us, her parents, looking after her from the side, her days there shouldn't be too difficult."

chapters.title: Entering the Mansion
chapters.content:
Qiao shi covered her face with a handkerchief and bit her lip tightly. Did that man have a heart?

He spoke so nicely, but her daughter was the legitimate eldest daughter of the Bo Marquis's family, raised in the palm of her hand, cherished and pampered, like a delicate flower just about to bloom. Yet, for the sake of the family, she was being forced into a life of widowhood, spending her days alone, guarding a man's spirit tablet.

Meanwhile, Su shi's daughter was about to be recognized and return to the Bo Marquis's family as a noble miss, eventually marrying with great fanfare and enjoying all the benefits that came with the Bo Marquis's status. How was that fair?

Soon, Qiao shi calmed herself and put down the handkerchief. "This concubine understands. Now the entire capital is praising the loyalty of the General's family. Countless people are watching to see how our Bo Marquis's family will respond. Even if this concubine is unwilling, she must marry off a daughter.

It's just that my poor Qingyan, at such a young age, must sacrifice her entire life for the family's reputation. The thought alone is unbearable."

Qiao shi spoke with such sorrow that Yu Jingcheng also felt a pang of guilt. He spoke to console her, "Naturally, I am also reluctant to let Qingyan marry. Just now, when Mother mentioned this matter, she was also extremely unwilling and felt guilty towards Qingyan. But His Majesty has already spoken; the Bo Marquis's family has no way out. Now, we can only wrong Qingyan."

Qiao shi nodded sorrowfully. "This concubine understands. This is Qingyan's fate; this concubine blames no one."

The more Qiao shi said this, the more Yu Jingcheng felt indebted to her and her daughter. He sighed and asked, "When is the date set?"

Qiao shi: "The ninth day of the tenth month."

Yu Jingcheng's eyebrows furrowed tightly. Wasn't that only a month away?

He took out several silver notes from his bosom and placed them on the table. "This is a silver note for ten thousand taels. Consider it a small token of affection from this father. Besides the dowry provided by the family, Madam, please prepare more fields, properties, and shops for Qingyan. After she marries, as long as this father is alive, I will support her in everything."

For now, this was all he could do for his daughter.

Qiao shi looked at the stack of silver notes in front of her and said gratefully to her husband, "Then this concubine will thank the Marquis on Qingyan's behalf for his kindness."

Yu Jingcheng watched Qiao shi's grief-stricken appearance and felt a pang of distress. This wife was someone his mother had chosen for him years ago. Back then, he had been so focused on finding Chengniang that he had neglected Qiao shi for a period.

After finding Chengniang, he had been stationed away from home, so he hadn't spent much time with Qiao shi. To say there were deep feelings between them would be an overstatement.

However, she was still his wife, married through proper rites, and the current mistress of the Bo Marquis's household. Over the years, the Bo Marquis's family, inside and out, had been managed by her. Moreover, she had borne him children. As his mother had said, even if Qiao shi had no merits, she had endured hardships.

Thinking of this, the words he had intended to say stuck in his throat.

Qiao shi covered her face with the handkerchief and cried bitterly. Through the gaps in the handkerchief, she secretly glanced at Yu Jingcheng and naturally saw the conflict on his face, which filled her with silent resentment.

She put down the handkerchief and slowly said, "I heard that Sister Su has already returned to the capital. Why hasn't my lord brought her back to the mansion? And what about her two children? They must be as outstanding as dragons and phoenixes. Since they have already returned to the capital, how can my lord bear to let them live outside?

For so many years, Sister Su and my lord have shared a deep marital bond. My lord even refused to return home for her sake. I do not blame my lord; I only regret that I am not good enough. Now that Sister Su is willing to return with the Marquis, it is a good thing. Naturally, the position of the legitimate wife should belong to Sister Su.

However, I am also a daughter of a good family and cannot bring myself to request to be a concubine. My father is a prestigious second-rank official, and I cannot tarnish the reputation of the Qiao family.

After much thought, I beg my lord to give me some time to properly arrange Qingyan's marriage. After she is married off, I will step down from my position as the mistress of the household and move to the ancestral temple. From then on, I will light incense and pray to the Buddha for the Bo Marquis's family and the Old Madam, and also seek the Bodhisattva's blessings for my poor daughter."

By this point, Qiao shi was sobbing uncontrollably.

Yu Jingcheng already felt guilty towards his daughter, and Qiao shi's words made him feel even softer. He increasingly felt that he had wronged this wife and his daughter, who was about to sacrifice herself for the family.

After a long sigh, he said, "Who said anything about making you request to be a concubine? And as for moving to the ancestral temple, do not speak of it again. Do not overthink it. Chengniang is currently staying at the Su residence to observe mourning rites for her parents-in-law. Regardless of whether she returns to the mansion in the future, you are still the Madam of the Bo Marquis's family. The entire household is under your management."

In the end, he did not bring up the matter of elevating a concubine to the status of a wife. He would deal with that later.

Qiao shi, with tears in her eyes, looked at him and said, "These are my lord's own words. I will remember them."

The atmosphere in the room remained sorrowful but not without rationality. Qiao shi had successfully made her husband feel deep guilt towards her and her daughter.

The next morning, a carriage from the Bo Marquis's mansion stopped in front of the old Su residence on Liuli Alley. It had come to pick up Yu Qingci and her younger brother, Yu Qingbai.

Originally, Old Madam Zhang had intended to send the steward to pick them up, but Yu Jingcheng, disregarding his mother's objections, had come personally.

The siblings reluctantly bade farewell to their mother and boarded the carriage.

Soon, they arrived at the Bo Marquis's mansion. The siblings followed their father, walking neither too fast nor too slow, side by side. Along the way, the servants they encountered all stopped to bow to them.

The closer they got to the Shouyin Hall, the more servants they encountered. Yu Qingci knew that this was just Qiao shi's way of asserting dominance, trying to use the grandeur and prosperity of the Bo Marquis's family to intimidate them first.

However, in her previous life, she had not been fooled by such petty tricks, let alone now.

Although they had grown up far from the capital's bustling life with their father and mother, their father came from a noble and distinguished family. In terms of education, upbringing, and daily necessities, he had raised them according to the standards of a prominent family.

Their mother also came from an official family and had been carefully raised from a young age. Her vision and knowledge were in no way inferior to the noble ladies of the capital; in fact, she had been outstanding among them. Otherwise, the then-Prince Yu Jingcheng would not have fallen in love with her at first sight.

Therefore, the siblings had been well-educated and were not intimidated by the current display.

The siblings showed no signs of fear or hesitation on their faces; they did not even look around much.

Soon, they arrived at the Shouyin Hall, where Old Madam Zhang resided.

As they entered the main hall, Yu Qingci looked up and saw that quite a few people had gathered.

Old Madam Zhang was dressed elegantly and sat upright in the center on a rosewood armchair, looking at the three of them with a gloomy expression as they entered.

On either side of the lower seats sat the masters of the Bo Marquis's family, all dressed in rich and exquisite clothing, adorned with jewelry, their hair decorated with jade and pearls. The faint scent of incense filled the room, making it feel particularly comfortable.

Numerous maids and servants stood around, holding their breath and standing at attention behind their masters. The entire main hall was so quiet it was almost intimidating.

Yu Jingcheng called out to his mother and then gestured for the siblings behind him to come forward.

---

chapters.title: Entering the Mansion (2)
chapters.content:
Two cushions had already been placed on the floor. The siblings stepped forward and knelt down in front of Zhang, kowtowing respectfully several times. Zhang's gloomy expression softened slightly as she sat there and accepted their greetings.

Because of her extreme dislike for Su Chengniang, Zhang had not had a good impression of these siblings since she learned of their existence. She coldly watched as the two children kowtowed to her before letting out a light hum through her nose and saying:

"Rise."

The two stood up, and Zhang beckoned them closer. "Come here so I can take a good look at you."

Yu Jingcheng hurriedly gestured for them to go forward. The two walked properly to Zhang's side.

Zhang first examined her granddaughter. The girl stood straight, her expression respectful yet neither servile nor overbearing. Her hair was as dark as clouds, her eyes bright and teeth white. Her skin, though bare of any powder or rouge, appeared as clear and flawless as jade, with the unique tenderness of a young girl. Especially her pair of clear, dark eyes, which were as limpid and profound as autumn water.

She was indeed a beauty.

Zhang couldn't help but think that even her own eldest granddaughter, Qingyan, who had been raised by her side, was slightly inferior in appearance. Though this girl was still young, in a couple of years, she would surely bloom like a peony and outshine all others in the capital.

However, the girl's appearance greatly resembled her mother, Su shi, which only intensified Zhang's dislike.

She turned to look at the half-grown grandson beside her. He also had red lips, white teeth, clear eyebrows, and bright eyes. Apart from his eyes, which were almost identical to his sister's—both had those narrow, phoenix-shaped eyes—the rest of his features increasingly resembled her son's appearance in his youth. Zhang quickly felt a liking for him.

After carefully examining both children, Zhang said to her son, who was standing nearby with an expectant look:

"Hmm, both of them have good looks. Look at Bai's face, his nose and chin are just like yours."

Yu Qingbai immediately responded cleverly, "Thank you, Grandmother, for the praise. I am my father's son, so naturally, I resemble him. I often hear Father say that Grandmother is kind and loving, and that after we enter the mansion, we should listen to Grandmother and be filial to her. I will certainly do so."

The old lady's face broke into a smile. "Good, you are an obedient child. Bring the gifts forward."

Immediately, a wet nurse behind her stepped forward with a gift box.

Zhang had prepared two items for Yu Qingbai: one was a gold lock engraved with his name, adorned with a circle of small diamonds, heavy and substantial in the hand; the other was a silver necklace inlaid with green jade beads, a style very suitable for a child of Qingbai's age to wear. It was clear that Zhang was quite satisfied with this first meeting with her young grandson.

As for Yu Qingci, she only received a jade ruyi of moderate quality, and nothing else.

Yu Qingci accepted the jade ruyi, remembering that in her previous life, this was exactly what she and her brother had received, so she didn't mind at all.

She took out the return gift she had prepared for Zhang, a forehead cloth she had personally embroidered with the characters for fortune and longevity. For this return to the family, all the gifts she had prepared for her elders were handmade embroidery. As a junior, such a return gift was the safest and most thoughtful.

Zhang narrowed her eyes and carefully examined the stitching, then let out a light hum through her nose. It was unclear whether she disdained the quality of the work or had some other thought.

Yu Qingci didn't care about the old lady's attitude. She resembled her mother more, and in her previous life, the old lady had never taken a liking to her, even though she had always been respectful and cautious in her presence.

Zhang spoke, "Alright, go greet your mother. You have just returned, and there are many things your mother will need to arrange for you. From now on, stay by your mother's side and learn the rules properly. Our Bo Marquis's family is a century-old clan, and all children, whether legitimate or born of concubines, are carefully educated so as not to tarnish the reputation of the Bo Marquis's family in front of others."

As the old madam spoke, she looked at Qiao shi, signaling for the siblings to approach. Qiao shi sat there, straightening her back and smiling at them.

A nearby maid, with good judgment, placed two cushions in front of Qiao shi.

Yu Qingci bit her lip and tugged at her brother's clothes. The siblings walked over and stood in front of the cushions, bowing. "Qingci/Qingbai greets Madam."

Qiao shi sat upright, ready to receive their greetings, but saw that the siblings did not kneel down to kowtow. Her smile froze, and upon hearing their names, her expression almost collapsed. She wished she could make the siblings disappear from her sight immediately.

In prominent families, the distinction between legitimate and illegitimate children was strict, and this was reflected in their names. For children of the same generation, only those born of the legitimate wife could use the family's designated characters in their names. For example, in the grandson's generation, the legitimate children all had the character "Qing" in their names, while other illegitimate children only had single-character names.

For instance, the illegitimate daughter of the eldest branch was named Yu Lian, not Yu Qinglian.

How dare the children of that cheap woman Su shi use the character "Qing" in their names? And now, they stood before her, refusing to kneel and kowtow, clearly indicating that they did not consider themselves inferior to their mother. How could this not infuriate her?

However, Qiao shi was skilled at concealing her true feelings. If she made an issue of this now, she would be openly acknowledging the distinction between legitimate and illegitimate, which could easily backfire.

She quickly adjusted her emotions, stood up, and took one child's hand in each of hers, looking them up and down with a dignified and proper smile. "You are both good children. This mansion will be your home from now on. If you have any needs, feel free to come to me. As long as you are the Marquis's children, I will treat you all equally."

Seeing Qiao shi's amiable demeanor, Yu Qingci felt a deep sense of wariness. In her previous life, when she first entered the Bo Marquis's mansion, Qiao shi had put on the act of a kind mother, lowering her and her mother's guard, which ultimately led to their tragic fate.

Not this time.

Who couldn't act?

Yu Qingci looked at Qiao shi with an especially obedient expression. "From now on, Qingci will listen to Madam."

At that moment, a disdainful snort came from the side. "What are you pretending at? You don't even call her Mother. After all, children from outside are just uncivilized!"

Yu Qingci looked in the direction of the voice. Below Qiao shi sat two girls dressed in luxurious clothing. The older one was naturally Yu Qingyan, and the younger one, who looked about twelve or thirteen, had fair skin and wore a brocade dress, her hair adorned with hairpins embedded with small diamonds and pearls, looking radiant and jewel-like. Around her neck, she wore a gold necklace with a jade lock. She looked at the siblings with disdain and provocation.

This was Qiao shi's younger daughter, Yu Qingying.

"Qingying, do not be rude. This is your third elder sister. From now on, your ranking will also move back one," Qiao shi said, looking at her daughter with a warning in her eyes, though her voice remained gentle.

Yu Qingying was clearly dissatisfied. She looked at Zhang and said, "It's them who have no manners. What did I say wrong? Why doesn't she kneel and kowtow to Mother?"

Zhang's face darkened like ink. Just as she was about to order the siblings to kneel and pay their respects, Yu Jingcheng frowned and reprimanded, "Enough! I see that it is you who lacks manners. Who taught you to be so disrespectful?"

chapters.title: Entering the Mansion 3
chapters.content:
Yu Qingying rarely saw her father, and his imposing presence always filled her with awe. Now, seeing him reprimand her, her small face paled, and she lowered her head, not daring to make a sound.

Madame Qiao, noticing this, quickly had someone bring out the gifts she had prepared. For Yu Qingci, there was a set of pearl hair ornaments. The pearls were not large, but the design was unique, each bead the size of a mung bean, with a soft pink hue perfect for a young girl. For Yu Qingbai, it was a set of fine brushes, ink, and an inkstone, the material and craftsmanship exuding an air of refinement.

Madame Qiao always conducted herself with generosity and grace in such situations, never appearing stingy.

Next, they paid their respects to the other elders: the fourth branch’s Madame Liu, who lived in the mansion, and the concubine-born daughters-in-law of the second and third branches, who had already moved out. The siblings approached each elder one by one to bow and greet them.

After the elders, it was time for the younger generation to exchange greetings. Today, only the descendants of the first and fourth branches were present. The second and third branches had only sent their two mothers-in-law, saying that all the grandchildren would come to meet each other during the evening banquet.

Madame Qiao had one son and two daughters. Her eldest son, Yu Qingyun, and Yu Qingyan were twins. Yu Qingyun was currently studying at the Imperial College and would only return in the evening. Her youngest daughter, Yu Qingying, was two years younger than Yu Qingci. Originally, she had been the third in the family hierarchy, but with Yu Qingci’s return, she would now be fourth.

Yu Jingcheng was often away on official business, but he occasionally returned to the capital to report on his duties. Besides Madame Qiao, the mansion also housed an old lady given by the dowager, Madame Wei, the mother of Yu Lian.

At this moment, Yu Lian was only nine years old. She stood timidly by her mother’s side, not daring to move or speak unless addressed. Her cautious and restrained demeanor was even worse than that of Yu Qingying’s maid, a far cry from the arrogance she had displayed in her previous life.

Yu Qingci glanced at her once before looking away. There was no rush. She would settle the score with her in due time.

There were also several children from the fourth branch.

Yu Qingci had prepared embroidered pouches or handkerchiefs with various floral and bird patterns for her sisters of the same generation, and for her brothers, she had personally made various types of braided ornaments.

Yu Qingyan and Yu Qingying were displeased to see that the return gifts they received were no different from those given to their half-sisters. Yu Qingyan maintained a faint smile, but Yu Qingying, being younger and less composed, immediately scowled, snatching the pouch and shoving it into the hands of a maid behind her. If not for the presence of elders, she would have given it away on the spot.

Yu Qingci kept a polite smile on her face. As long as she maintained appearances, it was fine. She did not want to waste her emotions on these people.

By this time, Dowager Zhang was looking tired. Yu Jingcheng dismissed everyone, as he had taken the day off specifically to help the two children settle in. He planned to personally take them to their assigned courtyard later.

Madame Qiao subtly signaled Yu Qingyan, who understood and stepped forward. "Father, you can just take my seventh brother. I will take my third sister to see the courtyard. Father, rest assured, I will take good care of her."

After saying this, she took Yu Qingci’s hand and smiled. "I have been looking forward to the return of my third sister and seventh brother. In the future, if my third sister needs anything, she can come to me. We sisters must get along well."

Madame Qiao chimed in, "Qingyan is right. That’s the way it should be. Qingci, go with your second sister. It will also allow me to take a break."

She then pointed to a middle-aged servant behind her. "Wu Mama is an old servant of mine. Let her go with you. If there is anything in the courtyard that displeases you or if the servants are not to your liking, just speak up. Wu Mama will report back to me so I can address it promptly."

Yu Qingci, of course, did not take Madame Qiao’s words seriously. She responded with a slightly shy smile, "Qingci thanks Madame. I appreciate my second sister’s kindness."

Yu Jingcheng, seeing this, was quite pleased. After a few more words of instruction, he left with Yu Qingbai. Yu Qingci followed Yu Qingyan and Yu Qingying, surrounded by a group of maids and servants, as they walked out.

Once they left the Shouyin Hall and were out of the elders’ sight, Yu Qingyan’s smile quickly faded, and she let go of Yu Qingci’s hand.

Yu Qingying also stopped walking. She turned to Yu Qingci with a contemptuous and arrogant look. "Hmph! A daughter from an outside concubine, and you dare to accept being called a sister? Where do you get the nerve? In this mansion, you had better know your place and behave yourself. Otherwise, I won’t mind teaching you what the rules of a noble family are!"

Yu Qingying’s voice was loud. Yu Qingyan frowned and whispered, "Say less. Don’t forget what Mother told us."

After that, she turned gracefully and said to Wu Mama, "Wu Mama, take her to the Wisteria Courtyard. I’m a bit tired, so I’ll go back to rest."

Without another glance at Yu Qingci, she left, followed by her maids and servants.

Seeing her sister leave, Yu Qingying smirked at Yu Qingci with disdain, lowering her voice. "Just a lowly-born bastard. Consider it your luck that the Marquis’s mansion is willing to take you in. Don’t think of yourself as a mistress. Wu Mama, take her to familiarize herself with the place."

With that, she too left in a huff, imitating her sister.

Watching Yu Qingying’s arrogant expression as she left, Yu Qingci recalled her fate from her previous life. It seemed she had married into a good family, but Yu Qingying, spoiled by Madame Qiao since childhood, had a willful and domineering nature. After marriage, she often quarreled with her husband and returned to her maiden home, causing a lot of trouble and giving Madame Qiao many headaches.

Wu Mama, standing behind them like an invisible person, pretended not to notice the two young ladies’ behavior. Only when both young ladies had left and only Yu Qingci and Tong’er remained did she step forward to lead them toward the Wisteria Courtyard.

The Marquis’s mansion was a large, four-section residence. Having lived there in her previous life, Yu Qingci was somewhat familiar with its layout. However, as a newcomer this time, she pretended not to know the way and silently followed Wu Mama.

Wu Mama did not speak, leading the way in front. Along the way, she took many turns, choosing open, unobstructed paths, all under the sun. They passed through one courtyard after another, even walking back and forth across the stone arch bridge in the back garden several times, yet never reaching the Wisteria Courtyard.

Tong’er could not help but glance at her mistress.

Yu Qingci, however, coldly smiled in her heart. The Wisteria Courtyard was not remote; it took less than a quarter of an hour to walk there from the Shouyin Hall. Wu Mama was clearly leading her in circles.

But Yu Qingci showed no sign of this on her face. Wu Mama was Madame Qiao’s most trusted confidante, over fifty years old. At such an age, she was not afraid of the sun or long walks, and Yu Qingci and Tong’er, being teenagers, had even less to fear. The only concern was the risk of getting sunburned.

---

chapters.title: Entering the Mansion 4
chapters.content:
The two continued walking in silence. Suddenly, Wu Mama clutched her stomach and said to Yu Qingci with a pained expression, "Third Young Lady, this old servant suddenly feels unwell. I need to use the restroom. I’m truly sorry, but please wait here for a moment. I’ll be back quickly."

Without waiting for Yu Qingci’s response, she hurried away.

Yu Qingci watched Wu Mama’s retreating figure with a cold, expressionless gaze. Tong’er grumbled displeasedly, "It seems the servants in this Marquis’s mansion aren’t very proper. Even leading the way has to be so troublesome."

Yu Qingci did not respond, but her hands, hidden in her sleeves, were clenched tightly into fists.

Before they could say more, they heard footsteps behind them. The mistress and servant turned to see a young man in a satin robe walking toward them.

Although she had expected this, seeing him still caused Yu Qingci’s pupils to contract sharply, and her expression turned icy.

The newcomer was none other than Qiao Yuantao, her husband from her previous life.

In her past life, it had been the same, except the servant leading the way had been another of Madame Qiao’s maids. That maid had also found an excuse to slip away halfway, arranging for her and Qiao Yuantao to "accidentally" meet on the path.

This place was relatively secluded. Besides the two of them and Qiao Yuantao, there was no one else. They had indeed chosen the location well.

But Yu Qingci knew this "accidental" meeting was just an excuse for what was to come later. The real drama would unfold that evening, so for now, Qiao Yuantao would not do anything to them.

With this thought, she steadied her mind and took a few steps to the side, turning away and refusing to look at Qiao Yuantao again.

At this moment, she did not know him, so she treated him as a stranger and ignored him.

Tong’er, on the other hand, stood protectively in front of her mistress, trying to block Qiao Yuantao’s view of her, hoping he would pass by quickly.
