But things did not go as she wished. Qiao Yuantao stopped in front of them, first bowing politely with a gentlemanly demeanor before speaking. "Might this be the third young lady of the elder branch who has just returned to the mansion?"

Tong’er widened her eyes at Qiao Yuantao, wondering how he knew.

As if reading Tong’er’s mind, Qiao Yuantao’s lips curved into a perfect smile as he continued, "I am Qiao Yuantao, the nephew of the Marquis’s lady. I came today to visit my aunt. I heard from my aunt that my uncle was bringing back a celestial-like cousin to be recognized by the family. Seeing your extraordinary demeanor and unfamiliar face, I assumed it must be you."

Hearing this, Tong’er’s guarded expression softened. She turned to look at her mistress with a questioning gaze, but seeing that her mistress still wore a cold, unapproachable expression, she understood. She curtsied to Qiao Yuantao and said, "Greetings, Young Master Qiao. My mistress is tired from the journey and wishes to return to rest. Please, Young Master, go ahead."

Qiao Yuantao, however, did not leave. Instead, he asked, "Why is the young lady here alone? Has she lost her way and doesn’t know where to go? Although I am just a guest, I am quite familiar with the Marquis’s mansion. Why not tell me where you wish to go, and I can show you the way."

Yu Qingci finally spoke, her voice cold. "There’s no need. Please, go ahead."

Despite her icy tone, Qiao Yuantao showed no intention of leaving. He continued to make small talk, seemingly at a loss for words.

He could only see a small part of her figure, obscured by Tong’er, but even this glimpse made him unable to look away, as if he wanted to see her clearly through Tong’er.

Yu Qingci knew Wu Mama had not gone far and was likely nearby. She said to Tong’er, "Tong’er, since Wu Mama is busy, let’s find our own way."

With that, the mistress and servant ignored Qiao Yuantao and prepared to leave. Just then, they heard Wu Mama’s voice coming from the moon gate.

"Third Young Lady, this old servant is back. I’m truly sorry for making you wait."

As she approached, she apologized to Qiao Yuantao. "Young Master Qiao, I’m sorry for the neglect today. My mistress has been quite busy and cannot keep you company for long."

Qiao Yuantao responded politely, saying it was no trouble.

Wu Mama glanced at Yu Qingci before introducing her to Qiao Yuantao. "Young Master Qiao, this is the third young lady that our master brought back today. She is also the master’s own daughter, named Qingci. In a few days, she will be added to the family genealogy. From then on, she will be your cousin."

Qiao Yuantao’s voice grew even more gentle. "I had already guessed she was my third cousin. Now that we’ve formally met, I hope you are well, Cousin."

He then gave another perfect bow.

In front of Wu Mama, Yu Qingci could not afford to lose her composure. She turned slightly and curtsied, but kept her head lowered and did not speak.

Qiao Yuantao exchanged a few more words with Wu Mama before taking his leave.

Wu Mama watched his retreating figure and said with a smile, "Young Master Qiao is a scholar with academic achievements. He is currently studying under a renowned teacher in the capital and will take the imperial examination next autumn. With his talent, he is sure to pass and become a Jinshi. His future prospects are limitless."

Yu Qingci gave a faint smile and said, "It’s getting late. Please, Mama Wu, continue leading the way."

Wu Mama, seeing that she did not engage in the topic, gave a slight, hidden sneer before leading the way again without another word.

"Mama Wu, it seems we’ve passed this way before."

As they once again passed through a moon gate, Yu Qingci kindly reminded Wu Mama.

Wu Mama stopped and looked around, her face showing some discomfort. She chuckled, "Is that so? This old servant doesn’t remember. It’s the first time meeting the third young lady, and I was so happy that I wanted you to familiarize yourself with the various courtyards of the Marquis’s mansion, so you won’t get lost as a newcomer."

Perhaps from the exhaustion of walking, Wu Mama’s voice showed signs of breathlessness. Although she was a servant, as Madame Qiao’s trusted aide, she lived a comfortable life with small maids attending to her, and she rarely had such strenuous days.

Yu Qingci expressed her gratitude to Wu Mama. "Thank you for your consideration, Mama Wu. But if we pass those courtyards again, perhaps you could introduce them to me so I can remember them better."

Wu Mama’s face stiffened, and she forced a dry laugh before continuing to lead the way.

This time, they quickly arrived at their destination.

Standing at the entrance of the Wisteria Courtyard, Yu Qingci looked up at the three large gold-painted characters on the black background above the door. This was the courtyard her father had personally chosen for her. It was not far from the main courtyards in the front, and the houses inside were well-maintained and grand, with a layout that was both orderly and aesthetically pleasing, in no way inferior to the courtyards of Yu Qingyan and Yu Qingying.

Wu Mama gathered the servants of the courtyard to meet their new mistress.

There were not many servants assigned to the Wisteria Courtyard: a managing mama personally appointed by the Marquis, a senior maid named Siqin who had previously served Madame Qiao, four junior maids, and four servant women.

Including Tong’er, whom Yu Qingci had brought with her, that was all.

Most of these servants had been assigned by Madame Qiao, likely because she knew Yu Qingci would soon be married off to her own daughter, and thus would not stay in the mansion for long. Compared to the number of servants in her two daughters’ courtyards, this was nearly half as many.

Yu Qingci understood Madame Qiao’s intentions. She was not afraid of these servants disobeying her. Before any open conflict, these maids and servants would still be useful, and at least they served with some dedication.

chapters.title: Family Banquet
chapters.content:
After Wu Mama finished her duties, she politely asked Yu Qingci a few questions. Since Yu Qingci was new, she naturally didn’t make any extra requests, so Wu Mama returned to report.

Yu Qingci glanced at the servants still standing properly in the courtyard, said a few words, and dismissed everyone except Siqin.

Siqin was a second-class maidservant by Concubine Qiao’s side, and now that she was in Yu Qingci’s courtyard, she would naturally be promoted to first-class.

Yu Qingci shot Siqin an icy look, and the resentment in her chest surged again. Now that they met again, Yu Qingci wished she could rush forward and slap her hard, but she quickly calmed down and casually averted her gaze.

She had already seen Qiao Yuantao in the garden earlier, so tonight, this Siqin would surely try to make a move behind her back, just like in her past life.

Fine, then let her have her way.

Yu Qingci asked calmly, “You used to serve the madam, right?”

Siqin bowed her head respectfully and replied, “Yes, Third Young Lady.”

Yu Qingci: “Since you were by the madam’s side, I suppose you already know the rules for servants. Now that you’re my first-class maid, you must do your duty properly. As long as you don’t slack off and do your job well here, that’s all that matters.”

With that, she went inside, and Siqin hurriedly followed to attend to her.

After a simple lunch, she took a nap in the afternoon. By dusk, Siqin came in to say it was time to go to the Shouyin Hall for the evening banquet with Old Madam.

Yu Qingci left Siqin at the Wisteria Courtyard and took Tong’er to the Shouyin Hall.

When she arrived, she saw far more people present than in the morning. The originally spacious main hall now seemed a bit cramped. Besides those who had returned from duty or school, the second and third branches—both born of concubines—had also come with their wives and children.

Another round of introductions ensued, but fortunately, Yu Qingci had memories from her past life. Even though the number of people had doubled since the morning, it didn’t take much effort for her to remember them all. As long as she didn’t make any mistakes in etiquette, she would be fine.

In the center of the Shouyin Hall’s main hall, four large tables were set. The entire Yu family of the Eldest Branch took their seats according to seniority. Since Yu Qingci and her younger brother, Yu Qingbai, had just returned to the Eldest Branch, Nanping Earl specially had them seated at the main table.

Old Madam Zhang only glanced at them without saying anything, while Concubine Qiao wore a kind expression as she warmly urged the siblings not to be constrained and to order the maids behind them to serve whatever dishes they wanted.

The faces of Yu Qingman and her sister, Yu Qingying, who were seated at the younger generation’s table, darkened. Especially Yu Qingying—she wished she could stand up, drag Yu Qingci and her brother away, and take their seats beside her father herself.

But the siblings paid no mind to that. As soon as Yu Qingbai saw his sister, he gave her a sweet smile, and Yu Qingci felt at ease.

With their father personally looking after her brother today, no one would dare to intimidate him. That was good. If anyone had tricks, they could direct them all at her.

Earl Yu Jingcheng hadn’t seen his daughter for most of the day, so now that he saw her, he asked with concern:

“Qingci, are you satisfied with the Wisteria Courtyard? If there’s anything you’re unhappy with, don’t endure it. Tell me, and I’ll have the servants rearrange it for you.”

He spoke with confidence. He had personally selected that courtyard for his daughter, and even the furnishings inside were arranged to match her old boudoir in Youyang, all to make her feel comfortable and at home.

Yu Qingci smiled at her father. “Father has gone to so much trouble. Since Father arranged it himself, of course your daughter is very satisfied. The courtyard is quite large, the scenery is nice, and there’s even a swing set—it’s really fun. I just didn’t expect the Eldest Branch’s estate to be so large. This morning, when your daughter followed Wu Mama to the Wisteria Courtyard, it took a full hour to get there.

From now on, if I come to pay respects to Grandmother, I must have the maids wake me up early so I won’t be late for Grandmother’s morning greetings.”

Her words left everyone stunned. Wu Mama, standing behind Concubine Qiao, was so frightened that her face turned ashen, and she didn’t dare lift her head.

She had deliberately led Yu Qingci in circles around the Eldest Branch’s estate on Wu Mama’s orders. Anyone would think that a young girl who had just returned home and wasn’t yet officially registered in the family genealogy would be nervous and anxious upon entering such a wealthy estate, fearing she might do or say something wrong and become a laughingstock. Even if she were given a hard time, she would have to grit her teeth and endure it.

But who could have expected that this girl would be so straightforward and actually bring it up in front of everyone? Was she truly naive or just pretending to be?

Earl Yu Jingcheng’s expression darkened immediately. His sharp, sword-like gaze swept over Wu Mama. She instantly felt a cold gust sweep over her, and her body trembled as she dropped to her knees, kowtowing repeatedly to Yu Jingcheng while muttering:

“Master, spare this old servant! It was my fault. I was so happy to see Third Young Lady for the first time that I wanted to show her around the various parts of the Eldest Branch’s estate. I didn’t realize I’d lost track of time and made Third Young Lady walk so much. This old servant deserves to die, deserves to die!”

As she spoke, she raised her hand and began slapping her own face.

Yu Jingcheng remained silent, his face cold. The others at the table didn’t dare speak either. All that could be heard were the sounds of Wu Mama’s slaps. Concubine Qiao and her daughters’ expressions were especially unpleasant, and Yu Qingying even wished she could bury her head under the table in shame.

After all, Wu Mama was Concubine Qiao’s servant. After a while, Concubine Qiao had no choice but to speak up and reprimand her: “Wu Mama, have you gone senile? I only asked you to take Third Young Lady to her courtyard because I thought you were steady and reliable. But you couldn’t even handle this small task and made Third Young Lady walk in circles with you. If I’d known you were this useless, I wouldn’t have let you serve me in the future.”

Wu Mama, hearing this, slapped herself even harder.

Concubine Qiao then turned to Yu Qingci with a kind expression and said, “Good child, Wu Mama is probably just getting old and a little confused. She meant well and wanted to help you learn your way around, but she ended up causing trouble by forgetting the time. A servant who makes such a mistake deserves punishment. Let her slap herself a few more times to vent your anger.”

Yu Qingci looked at her with a puzzled expression. “But… Wu Mama did bring me there in the end, so she didn’t really do anything wrong, did she? From what Madam says, it sounds like she still needs to vent my anger, but I’m not angry.”

Concubine Qiao: …

Everyone else looked at Qingci in shock. Poor child—she really didn’t realize Wu Mama had done it on purpose.

Wu Mama, who was still slapping herself: …

Old Madam Zhang shot Concubine Qiao a displeased glance and scolded Wu Mama: “Enough. You’re old—be more careful in the future. Now get out.”

Only then did Wu Mama crawl up and slink away, thoroughly humiliated.

Earl Yu Jingcheng hadn’t expected his daughter to be bullied by an old, cunning servant on her first day back. He was furious, but when he saw Wu Mama kneeling and slapping herself, and considering she was an old servant under Concubine Qiao, punishing her too harshly would make things difficult for Concubine Qiao. So he held his tongue.

---

chapters.title: A Show of Force
chapters.content:
Now that Wu Mama had punished herself and Concubine Qiao had apologized to Qingci, Earl Yu Jingcheng’s expression softened. He said to Yu Qingci, “You are my daughter, which makes you a precious young lady of this Eldest Branch. In the future, if any blind servant disrespects you, you don’t have to endure it. Just go tell your grandmother, and she will certainly take your side.”

He then turned to Yu Qingbai. “The same goes for you, Qingbai.”

“Yes.”

The siblings nodded obediently at their father.

Concubine Qiao’s smile nearly slipped. The Earl had actually told them to seek Old Madam’s help instead of her, the mistress in charge of the inner quarters. This was a direct slap to her face.

The others, hearing the Earl publicly defend the siblings, couldn’t help but reassess them. Yu Qingci then said:

“I’ll remember, Father. But Grandmother is old, and I wouldn’t feel right bothering her with such small matters. I’ll just tell Madam instead. Madam is kind and will surely take my side.”

With that, she looked at Concubine Qiao with a trusting expression.

Concubine Qiao’s expression grew even kinder as she nodded at Yu Qingci. “Of course, that’s the right way to think. Today was my oversight, and I let you suffer. It won’t happen again. If you have any issues in the future, just come to me.”

With this display of maternal kindness and filial piety, everyone tacitly moved on from the matter and began eating.

Yu Qingci had just picked up her chopsticks when she froze. Why were all the dishes in front of her seafood—and mostly shellfish at that?

There were braised prawns, boiled prawns, chilled sea cucumber, and several large steamed crabs neatly arranged on a plate, their round, bulging eyes staring right at her.

As she hesitated, she heard Yu Qingman at the next table say with a laugh, “Third Sister, why aren’t you eating? It’s rare to have so much fresh seafood. We have Third Sister and Seventh Brother to thank for this. You two should eat more.”

After speaking, she signaled the maid serving Yu Qingci, who quickly used her chopsticks to place several large prawns onto Yu Qingci’s plate.

Yu Qingying also urged her to eat, though her tone clearly carried a hint of schadenfreude. “Third Sister, hurry and eat! These are all extremely precious ingredients, specially transported from the coast. Only a family like ours can enjoy them in the capital. I doubt you’ve ever had them in Youyang. Would you like me to teach you how to eat them?”

Yu Qingci understood—they were trying to embarrass her. They assumed that as someone from a remote place like Youyang, she had never seen, let alone eaten, such delicacies, and they wanted to use this to humiliate her.

If she really had never eaten them before, she might have been caught off guard.

Unfortunately for them, their plan was doomed to fail. Though Youyang was a remote, desolate place in the northwest, her father was a man of noble birth and the local Inspector-General. What kind of delicacies hadn’t she and her brother tried? Not only were river prawns and crabs sold near Youyang City, but even rare seafood had been brought back for them by their father.

So their behavior was nothing but petty.

Yu Qingci calmly picked up a large prawn and put it in her mouth. The little girls at the next table craned their necks, eyes wide, as if waiting to see if she would swallow the shell whole just to keep up appearances.

Yu Qingci chewed the prawn in her mouth, and somehow, she managed to discreetly spit out the shell. Seeming to enjoy the taste, she ate several more before putting down her chopsticks and saying to her father, “This prawn is indeed delicious. Father and Brother should try some too.”

Yu Qingying hadn’t expected this outcome, and her anger grew. She couldn’t stand watching the siblings enjoy their meal so calmly. She said, “Third Sister, try the crab too. You’ve probably never had such a large crab before, have you?”

The serving maid immediately placed a large crab onto Yu Qingci’s plate.

Yu Qingci put down her chopsticks and looked at the crab but didn’t move.

Yu Qingying grinned. “Third Sister, why aren’t you eating? Hurry up.”

She wanted to see how this little vixen, who was clearly pretending, would manage to eat the crab. She didn’t believe she wouldn’t make a fool of herself!

Yu Qingci looked at Yu Qingying with a puzzled expression. “Where are the crab tools?”

Yu Qingying blinked. “What?”

Yu Qingci repeated, “The crab tools? Don’t you people in the capital use crab tools when eating crab? How do you eat it then—with your mouth?”

Yu Qingying’s face turned red with rage. “You’re the one who eats with your mouth! You—”

Concubine Qiao quickly interrupted, scolding, “Enough! If you don’t want to eat, then leave. Don’t make a scene here. What kind of behavior is this? Is this how I taught you to conduct yourself?”

A few sharp words left Yu Qingying on the verge of tears. Her mother had actually scolded her in front of so many people—how could she face her cousins after this?

After reprimanding her daughter, Concubine Qiao turned to the servants and ordered sharply, “Hurry up and bring the crab tools! Serve Third Young Lady properly!”

The servants quickly placed the crab tools on the table. Yu Qingci, without hesitation, began to enjoy the crab. She even picked out some crab meat and placed it into Earl Yu Jingcheng’s bowl, saying, “Father, try this. The crab is truly fresh and delicious.”

Earl Yu Jingcheng, giving his daughter face, picked up the crab meat and put it in his mouth, not forgetting to praise his daughter.

Concubine Qiao forced a smile and said, “Qingci is such a steady and well-mannered girl. Just look at her table manners—clearly well-raised. It’s no wonder she grew up by the Earl’s side. She’s truly a delight. If Qingying could be half as steady as her Third Sister, I’d be grateful.”

With that, she personally stood up and used the serving chopsticks to place a few dishes that were farther away onto Yu Qingci’s plate.

Earl Yu Jingcheng silently picked up a bite of food and ate it. When the table quieted down, he put down his chopsticks and said to Concubine Qiao, “Qingying’s manners are indeed lacking. You should put more effort into teaching her properly in the future. We can’t have her embarrassing the Eldest Branch in front of others.”

His words were blunt, and coming from the head of the household, they carried weight—almost like a slap to Yu Qingying’s face. Unable to hold back, the young girl’s face turned red as she clenched her fists. Finally, she covered her face and ran out.

This infuriated Concubine Qiao, who quickly ordered a maid to follow after her.

The atmosphere at the banquet had become awkward. The Earl and Old Madam were clearly displeased, and no one dared to speak. The only sounds were the clinking of teacups and dishes.

Yu Qingci ate in silence, her heart a mix of emotions. In her past life, her mother had drawn everyone’s attention, so all the underhanded tricks were directed at her mother. She and her brother had been spared. But this time, her mother hadn’t entered the estate, so naturally, these people had turned their sights on her.

In the evening, Concubine Qiao brought Yu Qingman to Yu Qingying’s courtyard. Yu Qingying was still in a rage, having smashed a pile of porcelain in her room, her eyes swollen from crying.

This time, Concubine Qiao didn’t indulge her. She sat down and scolded her for a long time, but when she saw her daughter’s swollen eyes, her heart softened.

chapters.title: Scheming
chapters.content:
Qiao Shi sighed, looking at her eldest daughter and then her youngest before continuing her scolding:

"Look at the mess you two have made. On the very first day, you resort to such shameful tactics, and yet you still fail. Every move you made was countered effortlessly, and in the end, you only humiliated yourselves! Truly ridiculous!

How have I raised you? If you lack the ability, then restrain yourselves!"

Yu Qingrong sniffled, but upon hearing this, she refused to back down. "I only wanted to make her look bad. I didn’t really do anything to her. Who knew she’d be so petty? She even complained to Father about walking a few extra steps and had the nerve to mock us for not knowing how to eat crabs. She’s so arrogant! And now my sister has been scolded by Father. Father is biased too—we’re all his daughters, yet he only takes her side!"

"Blame yourselves for being less capable!"

Qiao Shi saw that her daughter still wore a defiant expression and was so exasperated she could have iron into steel. After a few more reprimands, she lowered her voice and said, "I never expected that the daughter raised by Su Shi would be so cunning at such a young age. Truly, one cannot judge by appearances. She seems gentle and harmless, but every word and action is flawless, leaving no room for criticism. From now on, the two of you must not provoke her."

Yu Qingrong bit her lip and argued, "Why not? Does she think she can ride over my sister and me? She’s just a daughter from a concubine who returned out of nowhere. She should be grateful to Mother for allowing her to return to the marquis’s estate and acknowledge her ancestry. She should be ingratiating herself with us, like that cheap Yunlian does. But instead, she’s been so arrogant since the moment she arrived. Anyone who didn’t know better would think she’s the legitimate daughter of the marquis’s estate!

I can’t stand it. Mother, think of a way to make sure she can’t be added to the family genealogy tomorrow. If she can’t be added, she won’t truly be a daughter of our marquis’s estate. Then let’s see how she can remain so arrogant!"

Qiao Shi poked her forehead sharply and scolded, "What nonsense are you spouting? Did you not hear a single word I just said? You are never to call her a 'concubine’s daughter' again. From now on, you will address her as Third Sister.

And if she can’t be added to the genealogy, how will your sister marry into the general’s family later? Tomorrow’s matter must go smoothly. Only when she is successfully added to the genealogy can I arrange the next steps. So the two of you must behave yourselves. Absolutely no more provoking that little wretch. Behave properly and act like good sisters to her. Even if you have to flatter her, you must make her get along with you. Do you understand?"

Yun Qingyan, hearing her mother mention her own marriage, suddenly understood the stakes. She quickly nodded and promised, "I understand, Mother. Don’t worry. I will get along with her. After tomorrow’s genealogy matter is settled, I will take the initiative to reconcile with her."

Qiao Shi, still uneasy, turned to her youngest daughter and warned, "And you must never call her a 'concubine’s daughter' again. If your father hears you, he will punish you severely."

Seeing her mother’s stern expression, Yu Qingrong could only pout and reluctantly nod.

Only then did Qiao Shi relax. She smiled and soothed them, "That’s better. Once you’ve coaxed that little wretch into lowering her guard and she takes your sister’s place in the general’s family’s bridal sedan, it will be better than anything else. Once she’s married off, her life will be ruined. Then we won’t have to do anything. We can just watch her suffer through her days in misery."

The two sisters, hearing their mother say this, both showed delighted expressions and nodded. "We’ll listen to Mother."

Qiao Shi’s face also showed a satisfied smile. So what if Su Shi held the title of the official wife? In the end, her daughter would still have to serve my daughter. Once her daughter is married off in her place, I’ll find a way to deal with her.

---

Yu Qingci, accompanied by Tong’er, returned to the Wisteria Courtyard. After dealing with the day’s affairs, she felt physically and mentally exhausted.

Siqin, seeing them return, stepped forward, bowed, and said, "Third Young Lady, you must be tired today. This servant has prepared hot water. Would you like to bathe?"

Yu Qingci nodded, instructing Tong’er to hurry the hot water. She then removed the pouch from her waist and casually placed it on the table before heading toward the bathing room behind the screen.

Soon, a voice came from inside: "Siqin, you’ve also had a long day. Go rest. Tong’er will attend to me later."

Siqin, hearing this, rolled her eyes. The room was empty at the moment. She gritted her teeth, walked to the table, picked up the pouch Yu Qingci had placed there, and quickly tucked it into her sleeve before turning to leave.

At the door, she met Tong’er, who was leading two little maids carrying hot water. Siqin said, "Third Young Lady said she doesn’t need me inside. She’s more accustomed to Tong’er’s service."

Tong’er nodded. "Then Sister Siqin, you should go rest. You’ve worked hard today."

The two exchanged pleasantries before parting ways.

Tong’er entered with the two little maids and filled the tub. After they left, she whispered to Yu Qingci, "Miss, the pouch outside is indeed gone."

Yu Qingci’s lips curled into a sarcastic smile.

Tong’er, confused, asked, "How did you know she would take it?"

Yu Qingci couldn’t explain the past life’s events, so she casually said, "She’s Qiao Shi’s maid. I was just testing her. Now that I know she’s untrustworthy, we must be more cautious around her in the future."

"Yes, Miss. Don’t worry. I will keep a close eye on her."

Tong’er nodded firmly.

Meanwhile, Siqin reached a dark corner of the courtyard’s veranda. After watching Tong’er and the others enter, she secretly let out a breath of relief. She looked around to confirm no one was there, then, without further hesitation, turned and left the Wisteria Courtyard.

After a comfortable bath, Yu Qingci changed into a comfortable middle robe and sat in front of the dressing mirror, arranging her appearance. Tong’er stood behind her, skillfully drying her long, beautiful hair with a towel, and asked, "Miss, you must be exhausted today. Once I finish drying your hair, you should go to bed early and rest."

This time, when entering the marquis’s estate, she had declined the other servants her mother had arranged for her and only brought Tong’er.

Back when they were still in Youyang, her mother had placed many servants around her, all with the standards and treatment befitting a legitimate daughter of a noble family. The mansion had a large number of maids and servants.

Before departing for the capital, her mother had dismissed most of the servants, giving them their freedom papers, and only brought a few willing to continue serving with them to the capital.

The few senior maids around Yu Qingci had reached the age for marriage. Her mother had generously allowed them to leave. In the end, only Tong’er remained as her personal maid.

Yu Qingci looked at Tong’er through the inlaid mother-of-pearl lozenge-shaped dressing mirror. This girl had been bought by her mother when she was very young and had served by her side ever since. They had practically grown up together, so Tong’er had always been loyal to her, with her heart and eyes only for her mistress.

Recalling Tong’er’s suffering in her past life, she felt a surge of complex emotions.

In her previous life, Tong’er had followed her into the Qiao family and endured much hardship. Yet, every time she saw her mistress being tormented by her in-laws, Tong’er would unhesitatingly step in front of her, bearing the family’s cruel beatings and insults meant for her.

---

chapters.title: Entering the Genealogy
chapters.content:
At that time, the words Tong’er said most often to her were: *Miss, don’t be afraid. I will always be by your side.*

After a few years, Qiao Yuantao had the audacity to ask for Tong’er. Her kind mother-in-law had also insisted that she voluntarily give Tong’er to her son as a concubine, otherwise she would be considered an unvirtuous and jealous daughter-in-law.

For Tong’er’s sake, she had refused their shameless demand for the first time.

But Tong’er still could not escape their clutches. One day, her mother-in-law had found an excuse to send her away, and Qiao Yuantao had forcibly taken Tong’er to his room.

In that cold-blooded family, the mistress and servant were isolated and helpless, forced to swallow their humiliation and accept their fate.

But soon after, Qiao Yuantao, for the sake of his official career, had callously gotten Tong’er drunk and sent her to his superior’s bed. When Tong’er woke up, she had knelt in front of her, tears streaming down her face, and kowtowed three times. That very night, she had thrown herself into a well and died.

Now, looking at the living, breathing Tong’er in front of her, Yu Qingci hated her past self for being too weak to protect this girl. She couldn’t help but feel the urge to cry.

"Miss, what’s wrong? Did someone bully you today?"

Seeing Yu Qingci’s reddened eyes, Tong’er anxiously asked her.

Yu Qingci gently shook her head and casually said, "No one bullied me. I just miss Mother a little. I wonder what she’s doing alone right now?"

Tong’er comforted her, "Miss, don’t worry about Madam. With the Marquis outside taking care of her, Madam’s days won’t be bad. Madam instructed me to always stay by your side, Miss. Wherever you go in the future, you must take me with you. Otherwise, I won’t feel at ease."

The "Madam" Tong’er referred to was naturally Yu Qingci’s birth mother, Su Chengniang.

Yu Qingci smiled and nodded at her, silently vowing that in this life, she would ensure Tong’er had a good future.

And her mother and younger brother— in this life, she would protect all her loved ones.

The next day, the ancestral hall was opened for the genealogy registration.

According to family rules, women were not allowed inside the ancestral hall, so Qiao Shi could only stand outside with her daughters. Yu Qingci and her younger brother, as the day’s main characters, naturally had to enter.

As for Zhang Shi, she hadn’t even shown up. To her, the registration of two grandchildren into the family records was beneath her notice.

Watching the siblings follow their father into the ancestral hall, Yun Qingyan remained calm, but Yu Qingrong’s eyes burned with jealousy.

The ceremony was not complicated. After offering incense and kowtowing to the ancestors, it was time to open the genealogy and register their names.

Several clan elders who managed the family affairs were also present today.

Yu Jingcheng, bearing the title of Marquis of Nanping and holding an official position in the court, was not only the head of the marquis’s estate but also the clan leader. Naturally, he would personally write their names into the genealogy.

Yu Qingci looked at the genealogy her father had spread out and spoke at the right moment: "Father, do you intend to register my brother and me under Qiao Shi’s name?"

Yu Jingcheng paused and looked at his daughter. Yu Qingci continued, "My brother and I are the children of Mother Su. Father, you must see that clearly."

Yu Jingcheng sighed inwardly. In the genealogy, next to his name, the entry for his official wife was Qiao Shi. Back then, the old madam had acted swiftly and decisively, severing ties with Su Shi and her family. Not only had she made sure the entire capital knew that Su Shi had been divorced, but she had also persuaded the clan elders to remove his mother’s name from the genealogy.

It seemed that trying to smooth things over today would be impossible. His daughter was meticulous.

Yu Jingcheng hesitated before speaking, "Let’s first register the two of you in the genealogy. As for the other matters..."

But Yu Qingci interrupted, "Father, Mother is your original wife. Since we are opening the ancestral hall today, why not take this opportunity to restore Mother’s name to the genealogy? It will save future trouble. Although Mother is currently outside observing mourning rites for her parents and cannot return to the estate, you agreed to this, Father. As the official wife, her name should rightfully be in the genealogy."

In her past life, her mother had chosen to endure humiliation for the sake of allowing her and her brother to return to the family. In this life, she would never let her mother suffer such injustice again.

Faced with his daughter’s stubborn expression, Yu Jingcheng gritted his teeth and nodded. "Very well. Since the clan elders are all here today, let’s handle this matter together."

The several clan elders present exchanged glances upon hearing this. They were well aware of the circumstances surrounding Su Shi’s divorce years ago. The name of the marquis’s official wife in the genealogy had been changed under the old madam’s orders, with their assistance while the marquis was away. Currently, the marquis’s wife listed in the genealogy was Qiao Shi.

The eldest clan elder spoke up, "Marquis, the position of the original wife is of great importance. You must think carefully."

Yu Jingcheng addressed the two oldest clan uncles, "Second Uncle, Third Uncle, you two are most familiar with what happened back then. That divorce letter was not written by my own hand, nor did it bear my seal or signature. I ask you both to bear witness."

"This..."

The two clan elders exchanged a glance. After a moment of hesitation, they made their decision.

Over the years, the entire clan had relied on the marquis’s estate for survival. The current marquis was in his prime, holding both high rank and power. Normally, as long as it wasn’t a major issue that went against the interests of the entire clan, the elders generally followed the marquis’s lead without much objection.

Moreover, this was the marquis’s own family matter. It was best for them, as elders, to stay out of it.

However, in recent years, with the marquis often away from the estate, Qiao Shi, as the mistress of the household, had shown them proper respect and had never neglected the monetary gifts. Most importantly, the old madam was very satisfied with Qiao Shi as her daughter-in-law. Thus, they had turned a blind eye and let things be.

Now that they saw the marquis truly intended to change things back, out of both sentiment and reason, they still felt compelled to speak up for Qiao Shi.

Second Uncle tactfully said, "This matter is ultimately for the marquis to decide. We will all follow your lead. But marquis, please consider clearly whether Qiao Shi or Su Shi should be the official wife. After all, it’s not good for the genealogy to be changed back and forth."

Third Uncle added, "If Su Shi is to be the original wife, then what of Qiao Shi? Over the years, Qiao Shi has managed the marquis’s estate with care, serving her mother-in-law above and raising the younger generation below. She has not committed any serious errors. Surely she cannot be left without a proper title or status?"

The other elders also chimed in agreement.

Yu Jingcheng’s expression remained solemn as he addressed everyone, "I have already considered this carefully. Su Shi’s status as the original wife has never changed. As for Qiao Shi, she will be established as a secondary wife. The three children born to her will still be considered legitimate, and she will continue to manage the household affairs. In terms of status, there will be no distinction. This way, Qiao Shi will not be wronged."

Hearing this, the crowd had no choice but to accept. They nodded in agreement.

Seeing that no one else raised any objections, Yu Jingcheng dipped his brush and wrote in the genealogy.

Watching her father rewrite her mother’s name in the genealogy, Yu Qingci finally let out a sigh of relief. In this life, let’s see how Qiao Shi would try to suppress her mother.

Next were the two siblings. Under the witness of the clan elders, the names of Yu Qingci and Yu Qingbai were officially inscribed in the genealogy:

Yu Qingci, third legitimate daughter, born of the official wife, Madam Su Chengniang;

Yu Qingbai, seventh legitimate son, born of the official wife, Madam Su Chengniang;

From this day forward, Yu Qingci and Yu Qingbai were the legitimate son and daughter of the eldest branch.

chapters.title: Paying Respects
chapters.content:
Because the old madam was still alive, the grandchildren of the elder branch in the family genealogy were ranked together across all four houses, including the already separated second and third branches. This meant that among the elder branch’s grandchildren, including both legitimate and concubine-born, there were over a dozen in total. Yu Qingci ranked third, and Yu Qingbai ranked seventh.

The dust settled, and the crowd filed out of the ancestral hall one by one.

When Qiao-shi learned of this outside, her heart instantly plunged into an ice cellar, her entire body trembling with cold.

In the end, she had still underestimated Su-shi’s position in the master’s heart. In full view of everyone, she, the respected madam of the elder branch, had been reduced to the status of a co-wife. Qiao-shi wished she could faint on the spot.

She had feared there might be some trouble when the genealogy was updated today, so she had taken the precaution of bribing several clan elders in advance, hoping that if anything went wrong, they would speak in her favor.

But who could have expected this outcome? There hadn’t even been room for negotiation.

Qiao-shi looked at the elders with tears in her eyes. The few who had accepted her favors lowered their heads guiltily.

They had tried to help. Just now, in the ancestral hall, they had spoken up for her. But the master had always been a man of his word—once he made up his mind, it was nearly impossible to change. And they couldn’t openly defy him; after all, the master was the greatest reliance of the clan.

Yu Jingcheng turned to Qiao-shi. “Madam, the title of co-wife may be a slight to you, but after all, Su-shi entered the household first. You were well aware of the situation when you married into the Yu family—we never hid it from the Qiao family. Though you now hold the rank of co-wife, the management of the household affairs will still be in your hands. Your position in the household remains unchanged. In the future, I will still rely on you to oversee the entire elder branch.”

Yu Jingcheng’s words were polished, and at the end, he even bowed to Qiao-shi. In front of everyone, even if she was unwilling, Qiao-shi knew she couldn’t lose her temper with the master. She could only force herself to ask, “Does the old madam know of your decision?”

Yu Jingcheng replied, “I will explain it to the old madam myself shortly.”

The clan elders took their leave, and Yu Jingcheng personally saw them off. Soon, only Qiao-shi and her people remained in front of the ancestral hall.

Once they were gone, Qiao-shi felt her strength leave her, nearly collapsing where she stood.

She barely managed to return to her own Hai Tang Courtyard. After dismissing her servants and even sending away her two daughters, she could no longer contain her rage and grievance. She smashed an entire room’s worth of porcelain and ornaments, cursing like a madwoman, swearing that she would never let that mother and daughter have a good life.

After seeing the elders off, Yu Jingcheng went to Shouyin Hall to personally report the matters of the ancestral hall to Madam Zhang. As expected, she flew into a rage.

Yu Jingcheng listened in silence, offering no defense. After his mother had finished scolding him, he calmly ordered the servants to bring tea and personally attended to her.

Seeing him like this only infuriated Madam Zhang further. But apart from a fierce scolding, there was nothing she could do. She couldn’t very well call the elders back to reconvene the ancestral hall.

After the genealogy was updated, Yu Qingbai was to formally begin his studies at the clan school.

The Yu family, as a century-old aristocratic household, had many flourishing branches. With so many young men of marriageable age in the clan, they naturally operated their own clan school, staffed with several renowned scholars from the capital.

At Qingbai’s age, enrolling directly in a prestigious academy in the capital would still be difficult. So Yu Jingcheng decided to have him study at the clan school for a few years first, which would also help him cultivate relationships with his cousins.

Today was Qingbai’s first official day at the clan school. Early in the morning, Yu Qingci went to the front courtyard—there were some things she needed to remind her brother about.

Yu Qingbai was naturally delighted to see his sister come to see him off. He hurried forward and affectionately called out, “Sister!”

Yu Qingci corrected him, “From now on, you must call me Third Sister.”

Yu Qingbai stuck out his tongue to show he understood.

Yu Qingci said, “Remember what Father and Mother told you. Study hard at the clan school. And if anyone dares to bully you, or if you encounter a problem you can’t solve, you must come back and tell Father and me. Don’t keep it to yourself, understand? No matter what happens, you must never hide things from Father and me.”

Seeing how serious his sister was, Yu Qingbai nodded. “I understand. Third Sister, don’t worry. I am Father’s son—I won’t let anyone bully me easily.”

Yu Qingci was still uneasy. “You had better remember my words and take care of yourself.”

Yu Qingbai nodded repeatedly to show he understood.

*Sigh*, Father was right—women could be troublesome sometimes.

Before entering the household, Mother had also given him countless reminders, but her advice was the opposite of Sister’s. Mother had said that if anything happened, he should endure it and not cause trouble for Father.

*Sigh*, women really were troublesome.

Yu Qingci watched the small boy’s retreating figure and couldn’t help but recall the many hardships her brother had faced at the clan school in her past life.

From the moment Mother entered the household, Qiao-shi had set one trap after another for her, making the old madam dislike her even more. As a result, Mother had to be even more cautious in public.

Fearful that her brother would cause trouble at the clan school, she had specifically instructed him to be careful with his words and actions, to focus on his studies, and to avoid unnecessary conflicts.

But trouble had a way of finding him. Qingbai was intelligent and quickly won the favor of several teachers, which only made the other cousins resent him.

At first, Qingbai often returned from the clan school with injuries, and he gradually became silent and withdrawn. His academic performance began to decline.

Knowing how carefully Mother and Sister had to tread in the inner courtyard, Qingbai didn’t want to worry Mother, so he hid everything. If it weren’t for his young book boy secretly buying medicine for his injuries, which Yu Qingci had accidentally discovered, no one would have known he was being bullied.

Mother and Father had argued several times over Qingbai’s situation. Father had eventually reprimanded the cousins leading the bullying, and after that, they no longer dared to act so openly. Qingbai’s situation at the clan school improved, but the relationship between Mother and Father began to grow distant.

Later, Qingbai had gone with those cousins to a poetry gathering, where he had somehow gotten involved in a brawl. Someone had pushed him from behind, and his leg had been stomped and broken. From then on, Qingbai, like a bird with broken wings, had never recovered.

Father had only two sons. After Qingbai’s accident, Father had shifted all his attention and resources to his eldest son, Yu Qingbai, born of Qiao-shi.

So, from the moment she entered the household, Yu Qingci had never intended to let Qingbai stay at the clan school for long. The best course of action was to find him a good academy or a renowned scholar as a teacher as soon as possible, so he could leave the clan school early.

For now, this was only temporary. In this life, she would make preparations early.

After seeing her brother off, Yu Qingci finally went to Shouyin Hall to pay her respects to the old madam.

When she arrived, she saw that Qiao-shi and the fourth madam, Liu-shi, had already arrived with their respective daughters.

Qiao-shi’s gaze was icy, and Yu Qingyan was no better.

Yu Qingying, however, immediately recalled the embarrassment at the banquet and was about to make a sarcastic remark.

Yu Qingyan, standing behind her, gave her a light pinch to remind her not to speak. Yu Qingying gritted her teeth and forced herself to swallow the words on the tip of her tongue.

Yu Qingyan smiled warmly and took the initiative to approach Yu Qingci, taking her hand. “Third Sister, why have you only arrived now? Did you oversleep from exhaustion yesterday? Just now, Grandmother was even saying she feared you had lost your way and was about to send Sister Xichun to greet you.”

---

chapters.title: Paying Respects 2
chapters.content:
Yu Qingci naturally withdrew her hand from Qingyan’s tight grip and explained, “Thank you for your concern, Second Sister. Today is Qingbai’s first day at the clan school, and Father asked me to go to the front courtyard to see him off, which is why I was delayed in paying my respects to Grandmother. I ask for Grandmother’s forgiveness; it will not happen again.”

Madam Zhang had been annoyed that Yu Qingci was the first to pay her respects later than the other granddaughters. But upon hearing that it was her own son’s order—sending her grandson to the clan school—her displeasure lessened somewhat, though her expression remained cold.

Yu Qingci stepped forward to greet her and pay her respects. Seeing that her manners were proper and without fault, Madam Zhang didn’t intentionally make things difficult for her. She merely gave a faint “mm” and told her to rise.

But recalling what had happened in the ancestral hall the day before—hearing that it was this girl who had instigated the master, and that she had also humiliated Qingying in front of the whole family—Madam Zhang’s expression darkened once more.

Yu Qingyan secretly observed her grandmother’s expression. Seeing that her attitude toward Yu Qingci was neither warm nor welcoming, and even somewhat displeased, she felt a sense of relief. As long as Grandmother disliked this girl, her position in this family would never be a good one.

With her heart at ease, Yu Qingyan’s smile became even warmer and more natural. She stepped forward and said to Yu Qingci, “I’ve been meaning to apologize to you, Third Sister. That day, I had intended to personally take you to the Wisteria Courtyard, but I suddenly remembered I had forgotten to bring the shoes I was making for Grandmother. In my haste, I left early, which made you walk an extra distance. I’ve felt terrible about it. You don’t blame me, do you?”

Yu Qingci smiled faintly. “How could I? It was such a small matter that I had already forgotten about it if Second Sister hadn’t mentioned it.”

Yu Qingyan seemed to breathe a sigh of relief. “I knew you were a reasonable and understanding person. But it was still my fault, so I prepared a gift to express my apology.”

She took a pair of red gold filigree bracelets set with rubies from the maid behind her and placed them in Yu Qingci’s hand.

“These are a pair of ruby bracelets Grandmother gave me last New Year. They are quite precious. I feel they suit your temperament better, Third Sister, so I specially took them out to give to you. I hope you won’t reject them.”

Yu Qingci looked at the bracelets in her hand. They were gold, thick, and sturdy, with several rubies of excellent quality set into them. They were indeed fine pieces.

But suit her temperament?

These bracelets had been a gift from Madam Zhang to Yu Qingyan, her eldest granddaughter. Although they were valuable, Yu Qingyan had always found them too garish and had never worn them. Now, she had taken them out in front of Grandmother to give to Yu Qingci, both as a show of sincerity and because she didn’t truly value them.

Seeing that Yu Qingci had not reached out to take them, Yu Qingyan simply pressed them into her hand. “If Third Sister refuses, then you must still be holding a grudge over that day’s events and cannot forgive me.”

Yu Qingci weighed the bracelets in her hand. They were indeed quite heavy. Since the other party was being sincere, she stopped refusing and took them, saying, “Since they were a gift from Grandmother to Second Sister, they must be the finest. Thank you, Second Sister.”

Who would refuse free money? Such valuable jewelry was not to be rejected.

Madam Zhang, seeing the close sisterly affection between her granddaughters, was quite pleased. She spoke up, “Qingyan, you have a kind heart. The good things Grandmother gives you, you should keep them for yourself. Why go out of your way to give them to your third sister? Soon you’ll be married, and Grandmother wishes she could give you even more of her finest treasures from the bottom of her trunk.”

Yu Qingyan immediately put on a sentimental expression. “This granddaughter cannot bear to part with Grandmother either. After I leave, I hope Third Sister can help me fulfill my filial duties to Grandmother in my place.”

Madam Zhang’s heart ached even more at these words. “You are still the most filial granddaughter. No wonder I dote on you the most.”

She then turned to her close maid, Xichun. “Go fetch the pair of mutton-fat jade bracelets from my cabinet.”

Soon, Xichun returned, holding a pair of white, warm, and lustrous mutton-fat jade bracelets.

Madam Zhang personally put them on Yu Qingyan. The pearl-sized mutton-fat white jade beads looked stunning on the girl’s fair and tender wrists, so beautiful that one couldn’t look away.

Madam Zhang admired them with satisfaction, her gaze toward her granddaughter full of affection. Yu Qingci, standing to the side, suddenly felt that the red gold and ruby bracelets in her hand were worthless.

After comforting her eldest granddaughter, Madam Zhang turned her gaze back to Yu Qingci. “You should learn from your eldest sister. For women in the boudoir, gentleness and virtue are what matter most. You must not be sharp-tongued or domineering.”

Yu Qingci lowered her eyes submissively. “Yes, Grandmother.”

Madam Zhang coldly huffed. “For example, yesterday in the ancestral hall, you should have been grateful just to be included in the Yu family’s genealogy. You had no business speaking out of turn and disturbing your father’s mind, harming your mother, Qiao-shi. Go kneel and kowtow to your mother to apologize at once!”

Madam Zhang’s words were clearly in support of Qiao-shi.

Yu Qingci, hearing this, calmly walked toward Qiao-shi and performed a junior’s greeting. “Greetings to Madam. It was all Qingci’s fault for being thoughtless. If I have done anything to displease Madam, I ask for your forgiveness.”

Qiao-shi, seeing her putting on this unaffected act in front of her, wished she could slap her across the face. But she maintained her usual gentle and virtuous demeanor. “You’re overthinking, child. Please rise.”

Madam Zhang, seeing that she had not knelt or kowtowed, grew even angrier. She slammed the table. “How dare you! Did you not hear me tell you to kneel and kowtow to your mother?”

Yu Qingci looked puzzled. “This granddaughter has always heard that in noble families, propriety and etiquette are most important. Does a child of the original wife need to perform the kowtow to their father’s co-wife? If Grandmother says it is so, then this granddaughter will certainly obey.”

Madam Zhang was left speechless.

If she dared to say yes, it would be a joke.

A co-wife, no matter how you dressed it up, was still a co-wife. In the eyes of the world, she was a wife, but not the primary one. The children of a co-wife had to address the original wife as Mother and perform the kowtow, but the children of the original wife did not have to do the same for the co-wife.

Now that the genealogy had been settled, Madam Zhang had no choice but to accept it, no matter how unwilling she was.

Madam Zhang, choking on her words, turned to Qiao-shi instead. “The Third Girl was raised outside, so it’s only natural that she lacks some understanding of the rules and etiquette of the capital’s noble families. Qiao-shi, in the future, you must pay more attention to her upbringing. If necessary, rehire the tutoring mamas you previously engaged for the other girls to give the Third Girl some extra lessons.

I don’t expect her to be as poised and well-mannered as Qingyan, but at the very least, she shouldn’t disgrace the reputation of the Nanping Marquis’s household when she goes out in the future.”

Madam Zhang’s original intention was to reprimand Qingci, so her words were undeniably harsh.

Qiao-shi and the others, hearing this, were secretly pleased. They quickly stood up. “Yes, Old Madam. Now that the Third Girl has been entered into the genealogy, she is a proper young lady of our household. This daughter-in-law will naturally not neglect her education.

However, the tutoring mamas we previously hired were once attendants to the imperial concubines. Many noble families competed to hire them, and as soon as they left our household, they were taken by another family. I’m afraid it will be difficult to bring them back now.”

chapters.title: Paying Respects 3
chapters.content:
Qiao Shi changed the subject: "But the daughter-in-law will pay attention. Once a suitable governess is found, she will definitely invite her back to the mansion. Even if not for the third young lady, the fourth and fifth young ladies below also need careful upbringing.

As for now, the Wu Mama by my side has some skill in educating young ladies. How about temporarily having Wu Mama teach the third young lady some basic rules and etiquette first? Then we can discuss it again once we’ve invited a proper governess. What do you think, Mother?"

Madame Zhang nodded upon hearing this: "You handle this matter as you see fit."

Seeing her mother-in-law’s attitude, Qiao Shi felt somewhat reassured.

It seemed the old madam didn’t care much for this Yu Qingci girl. That was good. A little wretch about to be married off to the Wangmen family to become a widow—how could she be worthy of inviting a palace governess back to teach her? Didn’t she dare to put on airs in front of Wu Mama just because the elder master doted on her? Then let Wu Mama teach her a proper lesson about hierarchy and rules.

Yu Qingci waited for the two to finish speaking before saying: "Thank you, Grandmother and Mother, for your care. Actually, when I was at the Youyang ancestral home, Father specially invited a governess from the capital for me. Her surname was Li. This granddaughter studied under Mama Li for three years.

It was only at the beginning of this year that Mama Li’s health declined, and she wanted to return to her hometown to reunite with her family. Father and Mother, grateful for Mama Li’s teachings, specially arranged for someone to escort her back in honor."

Madame Zhang dismissed it indifferently: "That was your father being attentive to you as his daughter. But a common governess probably doesn’t have much skill."

Yu Qingci: "I remember Father once said that Mama Li had previously taught two princesses and one prince’s consort in the capital, as well as several young ladies from noble families. As long as I studied diligently under Mama Li, even if I only learned the basics, it would benefit me greatly in the future."

Madame Zhang and Qiao Shi both froze after hearing this. Madame Zhang asked: "Is this what your father said?" Yu Qingci nodded.

Madame Zhang asked again: "Do you know Mama Li’s full name?"

Yu Qingci shook her head: "This granddaughter does not, but I heard Father say that one of the two princesses Mama Li taught was Princess Minghua."

Silence fell over the hall once more.

Princess Minghua’s status might not have been clear to Yu Qingci when she first arrived in the capital, but these people naturally understood. She was the beloved daughter of the current empress dowager, one of the most noble princesses of the royal family. Many years ago, she married the legitimate second son of the Duke of Wei’s family. Now, she lived in Minzhou with her husband, who served as a high-ranking official.

And Princess Minghua’s governess was indeed surnamed Li. Mama Li had served by the empress dowager’s side in her youth and had successively taught many royal noblewomen and young ladies from prominent families. She had a very good reputation in the capital.

Qiao Shi’s face almost couldn’t maintain its kind expression when she thought that the governess her husband had invited for this wretched girl was actually Mama Li. Her hands, hidden under her sleeves, clenched tightly.

He had fathered two daughters with her. If he had such connections to invite Mama Li back then, why hadn’t he thought of their two daughters?

Yu Qingyan and Yu Qingxuan were no better off. Yu Qingxuan blurted out:

"You’re lying! What kind of status does Mama Li have? How could she be willing to leave the prosperous capital to go to such a remote place to be your governess? When Father returns and exposes your lies, let’s see how you’ll explain yourself!"

After saying this, her expression turned smug again, convinced that Yu Qingci was deliberately lying.

Yu Qingci looked at her innocently: "There’s no need to lie about this. If you don’t believe me, you can ask Father in detail when he returns."

Madame Zhang’s expression was also unnatural now. If this girl was telling the truth, then their earlier suggestion to have Wu Mama teach her...

Forget it. It was better to wait until her son returned in the evening and ask him for clarification.

So she said: "In that case, there’s no rush to find a governess for the third young lady. I’ll ask the elder master later."

Qiao Shi forced a smile: "Then we’ll listen to Mother. But this daughter-in-law has another matter to discuss with Mother. Normally, for the third young lady and Qingbai to acknowledge their ancestors and return to the family, our mansion should host a banquet to invite the good families of the capital and formally introduce them to relatives and friends. However, our Ber mansion is already the center of attention due to Qingyan’s marriage. This daughter-in-law thinks it’s better to keep a low profile for now, so we’ll have to trouble the third young lady and Qingbai for the time being."

Madame Zhang, reminded by her, immediately shifted her attention back to Yu Qingyan. She sighed and looked at Yu Qingyan with affection: "My poor first granddaughter. Clearly of noble birth, with looks, temperament, and talent that are in no way inferior to other noble ladies in the capital, yet in the end, she’s saddled with such a marriage. It’s truly a tragedy."

Madame Zhang’s resentment toward the Ningyuan General’s family grew even stronger. If it weren’t for them relentlessly forcing Qingyan to marry into their family to become a widow for their deceased son, why would the Ber mansion have to sacrifice their legitimate eldest daughter?

Qiao Shi lowered her head and wiped her tears: "Who says otherwise? But what can we do? Even His Majesty is on the general’s family’s side. It’s just a pity for my Yan’er."

Madame Zhang, holding Yu Qingyan’s hand, was overcome with grief.

Yu Qingyan quickly leaned forward to comfort her: "Grandmother, please don’t be sad. Things have come to this, and this granddaughter doesn’t blame anyone. This granddaughter will take on the responsibility. I only hope that Grandmother and Mother take good care of yourselves."

"Good child, you’ve truly been wronged."

Madame Zhang held Yu Qingyan and cried sincerely. After a long time, under everyone’s comfort, she finally calmed down a bit. She quickly called Xichun into the inner room, took out a stack of silver notes, and stuffed them into Qiao Shi’s hands:

"For once, I’ll show favoritism. These silver notes are this grandmother’s heartfelt gift. Take them and add them to Qingyan’s dowry. This marriage has already made the child suffer enough. The dowry must be generous to save face. If anyone is dissatisfied, let them come and say it to my face."

As Madame Zhang said the last sentence, her expression turned stern as she swept her gaze over everyone.

No one in the room dared to contradict Madame Zhang at this moment. They all wisely followed her words with a few compliments.

Yu Qingci stood to the side, her head lowered, not daring to show the slightest discontent. If she didn’t know Qiao Shi and her daughter’s plans, she might have believed that Yu Qingyan truly intended to marry into that family.

But this method of extorting money was quite good. Look, in just a short while, she had coaxed the old madam into giving out jewelry and silver notes. She wondered, when the bride was replaced by herself, would all those dowry items also be given to her?

Qiao Shi glanced at Yu Qingci out of the corner of her eye and thought to herself: You little wretch, enjoy your moment while it lasts.

---

chapters.title: Catching the Thief
chapters.content:
That night, the west wind was cold outside, but inside the room, candles lit up the space. The peacock blue glazed incense burner placed on the stool in the corner emitted a faint, pleasant fragrance. All was quiet.

Yu Qingci held a soft bolster and leaned against the couch, softly talking with Tong’er. Siqin entered and said: "Third Young Lady, the wind is strong outside today. Why not go to sleep early? This servant will make the bed for you."

Yu Qingci raised her eyes and looked at her quietly. Siqin gradually became flustered under her gaze. Feeling guilty, she lowered her head and asked: "Young Lady, why are you looking at me like this?"

Yu Qingci’s lips curved into a slight smile: "They say beauty is best appreciated by candlelight. Upon closer inspection, Sister Siqin is indeed quite beautiful."

Siqin let out a slight breath of relief and replied with a perfectly measured smile: "Young Lady flatters me. It is you who possesses celestial beauty, making others envious."

Tong’er watched the two exchange compliments and felt like laughing. She stood up and interjected: "Our Young Lady is naturally beautiful, and Sister Siqin is also good-looking. Only this servant is barely passable."

The three chatted and laughed for a while before Yu Qingci got up from the couch: "Alright, I’m a bit tired. Let’s go to sleep early."

Late at night, Ziteng Courtyard was silent. A shadow appeared soundlessly at the door. A hand pushed, and the door was slightly ajar. Delighted, the figure quickly slipped inside.

Soon, Siqin’s panicked voice rang out from the courtyard: "Someone, help! A thief has gotten in! Catch the thief!"

At this moment, many servants had just fallen asleep. Siqin’s voice was very loud, and before long, all the servants in the courtyard had rushed out. The shadow, flustered, seemed unsure where to hide. Seeing the crowd approaching, it quickly darted toward the main gate.

Coincidentally, a group of patrolling matrons was passing by outside the gate, led by Wu Mama. Hearing the commotion, they rushed over and soon pinned the shadow down.

Wu Mama approached. The shadow struggled to lift its head and shouted: "It’s me, Wu Mama!"

Wu Mama came closer and was surprised: "Young Master Qiao Yuantao, how is it you? How did you end up in the Third Young Lady’s courtyard on such a dark night?"

Qiao Yuantao looked utterly embarrassed and lowered his head without a word.

The commotion in Ziteng Courtyard had already been reported to Haitang Courtyard. Qiao Shi, accompanied by a group of people, hurried over.

Seeing the scene before her, Qiao Shi shouted: "What’s going on? How did a thief get into Ziteng Courtyard? Someone, go to the front courtyard and notify the Elder Master!"

Yu Jingcheng had been staying in the study in the front courtyard these past few days. At Qiao Shi’s command, a servant immediately headed to the front courtyard.

Qiao Yuantao had regained his composure by now. Seeing Qiao Shi, he quickly broke free from the matrons holding him down, stood up, and respectfully bowed: "Aunt, it’s me. This is all a misunderstanding, a misunderstanding."

Qiao Shi was also shocked when she saw who it was: "Yuan’ao, how could it be you? How did you end up here? What in the world is going on?"

Qiao Yuantao hastily waved his hands in explanation: "Aunt, this has nothing to do with the Third Young Lady. I acted on my own accord because I wanted to see my third cousin. I was afraid of being seen and implicating the Third Young Lady’s reputation, so I snuck in under the cover of night. I didn’t expect..."

His face was filled with shame as he trailed off.

Wu Mama, standing nearby, exclaimed: "From what Young Master Qiao is saying, does this involve our Third Young Lady? Could it be that you and our Third Young Lady..."

Wu Mama covered her mouth, and the onlookers’ expressions toward Ziteng Courtyard immediately filled with gossip.

When Yu Jingcheng learned that a thief had appeared in the inner quarters of the Ber Mansion, he rushed over without even finishing dressing.

Seeing the large crowd gathered at the entrance of Ziteng Courtyard, Yu Jingcheng was startled again. He strode forward and asked: "What’s going on? Where is the thief? Has he been caught? Is Qingci alright?"

Qiao Shi quickly stepped forward, her expression somewhat inexplicable: "Elder Master, don’t worry. The person has been caught, but... there seems to be some misunderstanding. As for the third girl, I haven’t seen her either. She should still be in her own room. It’s truly strange. Such a big commotion outside, yet it didn’t even disturb the third girl."

Yu Jingcheng, upon hearing this, immediately stepped forward to enter Ziteng Courtyard.

But Qiao Shi stopped him: "Elder Master, why not first see who was caught?"

She then stepped aside, allowing Yu Jingcheng to see Qiao Yuantao standing to the side.

Yu Jingcheng frowned as he looked him over, feeling a sense of familiarity but unable to recall where he had seen him before: "Who is this? This is the thief?"

Qiao Yuantao, full of shame, stepped forward and cupped his hands: "Uncle, it is I, Qiao Yuantao. I’ve startled you and Aunt. It’s all my fault. Just now, I explained to Aunt that this was all a misunderstanding. Please, Uncle, hear my explanation."

Yu Jingcheng had been stationed away from home for years and rarely returned to the capital. He was only familiar with a few of the legitimate branches of the Qiao family, so he had no impression of Qiao Yuantao, a son from a concubine branch.

However, hearing the other address him as "Uncle" and claim to be a Qiao, he could more or less guess his identity.

Still, he asked Qiao Shi with a displeased expression: "Is he your nephew?"

Qiao Shi explained: "He is the son of my half-brother. My half-brother separated from the family many years ago and has had little contact with us. However, this child often remembers me, his aunt, and comes to visit. Since you, Elder Master, are often away, you naturally have no impression of him."

Yu Jingcheng nodded to indicate understanding, then asked belatedly: "But how did your nephew end up in the inner quarters at this hour, and even get caught as a thief?"

Qiao Shi sighed: "I just asked him. Yuan’ao said, he said..."

Qiao Shi looked as if she found it hard to speak.

At this moment, a woman’s voice rang out: "Father, has the thief been caught?"

Everyone looked toward the sound and saw Yu Qingci, dressed neatly, walking out of Ziteng Courtyard accompanied by Tong’er.

Yu Jingcheng saw his daughter and stepped forward: "Qingci, are you alright?"

Yu Qingci shook her head slightly: "I’m fine, Father. I had just fallen asleep when I was woken up by the noise outside. Hearing someone shout about catching a thief, I was startled and didn’t dare come out to see what had happened. Only when I heard your voice did I come out to look. Was there really a thief?"

She sighed and added: "I truly didn’t expect that in the heavily guarded Ber Mansion, a thief could still slip in. Father, you must investigate this thoroughly."

Qiao Shi coldly laughed: "I should be the one asking you. Our Ber Mansion has never had such an incident. How is it that as soon as you returned, a thief appeared in this courtyard?"

Yu Qingci looked at Qiao Shi in surprise: "Madame, what do you mean? Are you suggesting that I let the thief in?"

At this moment, Qiao Yuantao stepped forward, his voice filled with emotion: "Third Cousin, it’s all my fault. I only wanted to sneak in and see you. Who knew that as soon as I entered the courtyard, I would startle someone, and it ended up like this, disturbing Uncle and Aunt. I am truly ashamed."

He turned to Yu Jingcheng and Qiao Shi: "Uncle, Aunt, please don’t blame Third Cousin. It’s all my fault. I saw something that reminded me of her and couldn’t help but miss Third Cousin deeply, so I snuck in. I’ll leave now."

Qiao Shi said in disbelief: "What did you say? Yuan’ao, are you saying you snuck in at night just to see Qingci? But this girl has only been back for a few days. The two of you shouldn’t even know each other. What is going on here?"

chapters.title: Private Exchange
chapters.content:
Just then, Nurse Wu stepped forward and said, "Reporting to the Master and Madam, this old servant has something I haven’t mentioned to Madam. In truth, Young Master Jiao and the Third Young Lady have met before.

On the day the Third Young Lady returned to the manor, this old servant led the group back to the Wisteria Courtyard. Halfway there, I had to excuse myself for a moment. When I returned, I saw Young Master Jiao and the Third Young Lady standing together. At first, I feared the Third Young Lady would be displeased at encountering an outsider, but I saw them talking happily, so I set my mind at ease.

I just forgot to mention it to Madam—it’s all my fault. I deserve to die." As she spoke, she lightly slapped her own face in a show of self-reproach.

Tong’er, upon hearing Nurse Wu’s words, was so angry her face turned red. She couldn’t help but shout, "Nurse Wu, how can you spout such nonsense? When did our young lady ever have a pleasant conversation with your Young Master Jiao? That day, this servant was with our young lady the whole time. She didn’t even exchange a few words with him—how did it turn into a ‘pleasant conversation’ in your mouth?"

Nurse Wu replied, "I didn’t hear what Young Master Jiao and the Third Young Lady actually said. I only saw them from afar. You little girl, why are you shouting at me without knowing the full story? If you’re so sure, why don’t you tell everyone what they said that day?"

Tong’er, too simple-minded to catch the trap in Nurse Wu’s words, was about to argue again, but Yu Qingci pulled her close, signaling her to stop.

She wanted to see how Madame Qiao would play out this act today. As for Qiao Yuantao, she couldn’t even be bothered to glance at him.

Madame Qiao also said to Nurse Wu, "Enough, both of you. Stop making such a commotion. Let’s hear what Yuan’tao and the Third Young Lady have to say."

Yu Jingcheng’s expression darkened as he was about to speak, but more people arrived. Everyone looked and saw that the leading figure was none other than Qin Mama, the steward of Shouyin Hall. Without a doubt, Madame Zhang had been alerted as well.

Qin Mama approached, knelt before Yu Jingcheng and Madame Qiao, and said, "The Old Madam learned that thieves had entered the courtyard. She was so angry she couldn’t sleep. She asks the Master and Madam to come and explain, and to bring the captured thief with you. She wants to question him personally."

Madame Qiao naturally had no objections. Yu Jingcheng, seeing this, knew the matter couldn’t be easily resolved. He had to find out what was really going on, so he nodded in agreement.

Soon, the group arrived at Shouyin Hall.

Upon entering, Yu Qingci saw that her two sisters, Yu Qingyan and Yu Qingying, were already sitting with Madame Zhang. She couldn’t help but think to herself: *Perfect, everyone’s here.*

Madame Qiao, seeing her two daughters, opened her mouth and asked, "Why are you two here as well?"

Yu Qingyan spoke softly, "These past few days, your daughter has been busy with the embroidery work Mother assigned, so I rarely went out. Tonight, my fourth sister came to visit me, and we stayed up late chatting and sewing. Just now, we heard the noise outside and asked around. Only then did we learn that thieves had actually entered the Third Younger Sister’s courtyard. We were so worried about her that we came to check on her."

After saying this, she walked up to Yu Qingci, looking her over with concern. "Third Younger Sister, are you alright?"

Yu Qingci replied calmly, "I’m fine. Thank you for your concern, Second Elder Sister and Fourth Younger Sister. It’s kind of you to come all the way to Shouyin Hall to see me."

*Instead of going directly to Wisteria Courtyard.*

Yu Qingyan’s eyes flickered, as if only now noticing Qiao Yuantao standing below. She couldn’t help but exclaim, "Cousin Jiao, why are you here? Could it be that the thief in the Third Younger Sister’s courtyard is—"

Yu Jingcheng’s face darkened at once, and he coldly huffed, "Qingyan, as a young lady, you shouldn’t meddle in these matters. Your mother and I are here—it’s enough. Take Qingying back to rest."

But Madame Qiao spoke up, "Since so many people have seen what happened today, in my opinion, there’s no need to hide it. Why not clarify the matter in front of Mother? If it’s truly a misunderstanding, we can clear the Third Young Lady’s name and also let her sisters learn how to handle such matters."

Madame Zhang, already impatient, slammed the table and snapped at Madame Qiao, "How have you been managing the household? When has our manor ever had such a scandal? Where is the thief?"

Madame Qiao first apologized to Madame Zhang, then turned and gestured for Qiao Yuantao to step forward.

Qiao Yuantao immediately knelt beside Madame Zhang and repeated his earlier story.

Madame Zhang was also shocked. She already disliked Yu Qingci, and now her gaze turned even more vicious. "What is the meaning of this? Qingci, explain yourself!"

Yu Qingci calmly lifted her head, her smoky, beautiful eyes unreadable. "Grandmother, he’s lying. I don’t know who gave him the courage to falsely accuse me like this."

Qiao Yuantao, hearing this, grew flustered and blurted out, "Third Cousin, how can you say that? Have you forgotten that you were the one who showed interest in me first?"

Madame Qiao, seeing this, revealed a sarcastic smile at the corner of her eyes. She turned to Qiao Yuantao and said, "Yuan’tao, what do you mean by that? Just now, the Third Young Lady denied everything, but your words are completely different. Earlier, you even said things like ‘seeing objects reminds me of her’ and ‘I miss her deeply.’ Do you know the consequences of saying such things? What exactly is going on here? Could it be that you and the Third Young Lady have had other… *private exchanges*?"

At this point, Madame Qiao’s expression grew even more shocked. "Could it be that you two have been secretly exchanging gifts? Heavens, Master, what are we to do?"

"Enough!"

Yu Jingcheng’s anger burned even hotter upon hearing Madame Qiao and her nephew’s words. Frankly, he didn’t believe Qiao Yuantao at all. After all, Qingci was his own daughter, raised right before his eyes. Her nature and upbringing made it impossible for her to engage in private exchanges with a strange man.

Yu Jingcheng glared at Qiao Yuantao and roared, "You shameless wretch! How dare you slander my daughter’s reputation? You have some nerve! I’ll have you beaten to death on the spot! Guards!"

The moment the authority of a superior was displayed, everyone in the room felt an invisible pressure. Qiao Yuantao was so frightened he nearly prostrated himself on the ground, looking up in panic at Madame Qiao.

Madame Qiao quickly spoke in a conciliatory tone, "Master, please don’t be angry. I know my nephew—he’s not the kind of person to spout nonsense. If he said those things, there must be some hidden truth we don’t know about. Let’s hear him out first. We must find out the reason before acting.

If you punish him without knowing the full story, it won’t be fair when word gets out."

Yu Jingcheng glared. "What hidden truth could there be? Do you actually believe your good-for-nothing nephew’s lies? Qingci has only been back for a few days. Even if she *had* met this scoundrel, she couldn’t possibly have engaged in secret exchanges with him!"

Yu Qingci felt a surge of gratitude upon hearing her father defend her. In this room, the only one who believed her was her father.

In her past life, it had been the same—at first, her father had refused to believe these people and had defended her wholeheartedly. That was until Qiao Yuantao presented his so-called *evidence*, leaving her with no way to defend herself.

---

chapters.title: No Way to Defend Herself
chapters.content:
In her past life, this incident had happened after Yu Qingyan married into the General’s Manor. But in this life, it seemed Madame Qiao couldn’t wait and was trying to pin the reputation of private exchanges on her early.

Still, Madame Qiao’s current goal was probably to force her into a substitute marriage, not to push her toward Qiao Yuantao. So she decided to stay calm and see how they would play this out.

Madame Qiao urged Qiao Yuantao, "Explain yourself clearly in front of the Old Madam. Do not hide anything."

Everyone turned their gaze to Qiao Yuantao. Flustered, he said, "Uncle, Aunt, every word I said earlier is true. I have proof."
