With that, he pulled out an exquisitely patterned, pale yellow brocade pouch from his sleeve and held it up for everyone to see.

"This is the pouch the Third Cousin gave me. That day in the garden, I happened to run into her. At the time, she was in a hurry to return and rest, so we didn’t speak much. But not long after, this maid of hers, Tong’er, came looking for me. She gave me this pouch and said the Third Cousin had specifically asked her to deliver it to me.

The Third Cousin is naturally beautiful, and I was indeed moved when I first saw her. I never expected her to feel the same about me. I was overjoyed and accepted it.

I carried this pouch with me every day, tossing and turning at night, unable to sleep. I simply couldn’t forget her figure from that day.

But I know my place—I’m just a distant relative of the Jiao family, a mere scholar with no wealth. I know I’m not good enough for the Third Cousin. But I couldn’t let go of my feelings, so I took a chance and snuck in tonight, hoping to see her and ask for clarity. If she truly had feelings for me, I would never let her down—I’d even dare to ask Uncle and Aunt for her hand in marriage.

If she was just momentarily interested or outright denied it, I would never bother her again."

At this point, Qiao Yuantao looked at Yu Jingcheng and Madame Qiao again, his tone even more sincere. "Uncle, Aunt, it was my fault for causing such a scene. If you must punish someone, punish me alone. Don’t take it out on the Third Cousin."

Tong’er, unable to bear his false sincerity, shouted, "You’re lying! Our young lady never gave you any pouch, and she never sent me to find you! How dare you slander her with such nonsense? It’s despicable!"

Tong’er was so angry her chest heaved.

Qiao Yuantao looked ashamed as he addressed the crowd, "Miss Tong’er, if you didn’t personally give this to me, how could an outsider like me have obtained a pouch that belongs to your young lady? This pouch can’t be fake."

Madame Qiao took the pouch and examined it carefully. "This pouch seems familiar. A couple of days ago, the Third Young Lady was carrying one that looked just like this. Master, you might not have noticed, but Qingyan, Qingying—you two must have seen it, right?"

Yu Qingyan and her sister stepped forward to inspect it. Yu Qingying looked at Yu Qingci with a mocking expression. "Isn’t this the pouch the Third Elder Sister used to carry? I’ve seen it before. It’s the same brocade, and the embroidery is the same pattern she always uses. You can’t deny it."

Yu Qingyan also looked shocked, her gaze toward Yu Qingci filled with conflict, as if unsure whether to tell the truth. Yu Jingcheng’s expression darkened further at his two daughters’ reactions.

Madame Qiao then looked at Siqin, who was standing among the servants, and called out, "Siqin, you’ve been attending to the Third Young Lady these past few days. Come and see if you recognize this pouch."

Siqin stepped forward, took one look, and nodded. "This pouch—I’ve seen it on the Third Young Lady before. It must be hers."

Everyone turned to look at Yu Qingci.

Yu Jingcheng also looked at his daughter, disbelieving. "Is this really yours?"

Yu Qingci’s expression remained calm. She parted her lips and said, "No."

Madame Zhang was already furious. Seeing her denial, she loudly demanded, "You still dare to lie? So many people have seen you with this pouch—how do you explain that? Are you saying all these people are wronging you? Then tell me, how did your pouch end up in Young Master Jiao’s hands?"

Madame Qiao, on the other hand, looked at Yu Qingci with a helpless expression. "Qingci, I understand. Having just returned to the manor, you might not feel a sense of belonging here, or perhaps after meeting my nephew, you developed feelings for him. It’s not strange—after all, my nephew is handsome and a well-read scholar. Who knows, one day he might pass the imperial exams and bring honor to his family. It’s normal for you to have your own thoughts.

But a young lady’s reputation is of the utmost importance. You grew up in the countryside, so perhaps your mother didn’t teach you properly in this regard—"

When she heard Madame Qiao dragging her mother into this, Yu Qingci cut her off sharply, "Madame, please do not overstep your bounds by questioning my mother’s teachings. After all, my mother is Father’s original and lawful wife, while you… are merely a concubine."

"You—!"

Madame Qiao’s face turned ashen at these words.

Madame Zhang raged, "How daring! How disobedient! There’s no excuse for speaking to your elders like that in public. I think Madame Qiao is right—your mother clearly didn’t raise you properly, which is why you’ve done something so shameless and improper!"

Yu Jingcheng furrowed his brows tightly. "Mother, we haven’t gotten to the bottom of this yet. Let’s not jump to conclusions."

Madame Zhang shot him a displeased look. "You’re still defending her? The truth is right in front of us—this shameless girl has been exchanging gifts in secret with a man. What more is there to clarify?"

Nurse Wu quickly stepped forward to Madame Zhang’s side and gently massaged her back. "Old Madam, please calm your anger. The most urgent matter now isn’t educating the Third Young Lady, but how to handle tonight’s incident. After all, so many servants have seen what happened. Public opinion is powerful. If we don’t handle this properly, it could affect the reputations of all the young ladies in the manor when it comes to future marriage prospects."

Madame Zhang came to her senses. "Yes, yes, this must be handled properly. We can’t leave any hidden troubles. Qiao, Qin Mama—tonight, all those who know about this are under your supervision. Seal every servant’s mouth. If anyone dares to spread rumors outside, beat them to death!"

Madame Qiao replied, "Yes, your daughter-in-law will handle it perfectly. Not a single harmful rumor will spread. As for my nephew, I will deal with him as well. Mother, rest assured."

After saying this, she turned to Qiao Yuantao. "As for today’s matter, considering your mutual affection, as elders, we should naturally help you fulfill your wishes. But you must understand that Qingci is a legitimate daughter of the Yu family—her status is noble. Though you are my nephew, your father is from a concubine and has already left the family. Even though you have the title of *xiucai*, your future prospects, compared to the Yu family, are still a stretch. Not to mention Master Yu and the Old Madam—even I, her aunt, would not agree to this.

Moreover, marriage has always been a matter of parental arrangement and matchmakers’ words. There’s no such thing as privately deciding one’s lifelong partner. If word gets out, it will only bring shame upon us for being unchecked. Therefore, as your aunt, I will take charge today. Return the pouch the Third Young Lady gave you. From now on, control your mouth. Let’s pretend none of this ever happened."

chapters.title: A Substitute Marriage
chapters.content:
Qiao Yuantao lowered his head with a guilty expression. "Yes, I will listen to my aunt. Since my third cousin denies it, I will not trouble her anymore."

Madame Qiao nodded in satisfaction and continued, "This matter must never be spread abroad. Qing Ying is still young, and Qing Yan is about to be married. If any rumor reaches the General's Manor, they might not say anything now, but after Qing Yan marries, who knows how they will mock her. It breaks my heart to think that our carefully raised daughter from the Duke's Manor, after marrying into a family as a widow-to-be, will also suffer in reputation because of this. My poor child, how unfortunate she is."

As she spoke, she covered her face with a handkerchief and began to weep.

Madame Zhang, hearing this, felt the same and took Yu Qing Yan's hand, her voice choked with sobs. "My poor granddaughter, when has a daughter from our Duke's Manor ever done such a shameless thing? And now it will implicate Qing Yan. As her grandmother, it pains me. This third girl is so willful and has tarnished our reputation. In my opinion, no punishment is too severe for her. Confine her to the Wisteria Courtyard first, and after things settle down, we will punish her further. This time, she must learn her lesson."

She then turned to Yu Jingcheng. "This time, it is the third girl's own fault. Lord Duke, you must not protect or plead for her."

Yu Jingcheng sat there with a dark expression, silent, seemingly acquiescing to Madame Zhang's decision.

Madame Zhang continued, "Qin Mom, personally escort the third girl back to the Wisteria Courtyard. Order a few capable servants to guard the courtyard front and back. From today onwards, no one is allowed in or out."

Tong’er, hearing this, panicked and opened her mouth to plead for her mistress.

Yu Qingci pressed down hard on her hand to stop her from speaking. Just as she was about to speak herself, she noticed Madame Qiao glancing at Qin Mom out of the corner of her eye.

Qin Mom understood the unspoken cue and stepped forward, speaking softly to Madame Zhang, "Old Madam, please calm your anger. This old servant has an idea, but I'm not sure if I should say it."

Madame Zhang had always trusted Qin Mom and replied casually, "Speak freely."

Qin Mom said, "The third young lady is young and ignorant, and has made a grave mistake. No matter how we cover for her, so many servants have seen it. Over time, it's hard to guarantee that rumors won't spread and affect the reputation of the other young ladies in our Duke's Manor. In this old servant's opinion, it's better to cut the Gordian knot and marry the third young lady off as soon as possible. Once the third young lady is married, even if rumors spread later, first, the third young lady has not been back in the manor for long, so not many people in the capital know her. Second, since she is already married, the impact on the other young ladies in the manor will be minimized."

Madame Zhang's heart stirred. "That is a solution, but where can we find a suitable family at such short notice?"

Madame Zhang glanced at Qiao Yuantao, who was standing below with a look of disgust. Even if the third girl was not to her liking, she was still a daughter of their Duke's Manor. Qiao Yuantao, a son from a concubine branch of the Jiao family, was of too low a status to be a match.

Qin Mom saw her looking at Qiao Yuantao and knew she was on the wrong track. She moved closer to the Old Madam and whispered a few words in her ear.

The Old Madam listened and said, "What? You mean have the third girl marry to the General's Manor in place of Qing Yan?"

The Old Madam was not truly surprised by this suggestion. Before Yu Qingci and her siblings had returned to the manor, Madame Qiao had hinted at this several times. At that time, Madame Zhang had also wavered, but since the third girl had not yet returned, and she had been focused on how to deal with Madame Su after her return, she had not expressed her stance on the matter. Now that Qin Mom had brought it up again, Madame Zhang felt that this was the perfect opportunity to change the fate of her eldest granddaughter's marriage.

She turned to Yu Jingcheng, who was sitting there with a dark face. "Lord Duke, in my opinion, this is a good solution. What do you think?"

Yu Jingcheng had been sitting there, seething with anger. As a man, he was already impatient with such inner-chamber affairs. Now, to have Qingci involved in such a matter, his temper was at its limit. He would have liked to tie up Qiao Yuantao and beat him to death. However, since Qiao Yuantao was Madame Qiao's nephew, he could not do that. As he sat there, fuming, he heard his mother's suggestion and was taken aback. He blurted out, "How can this be?"

Deep down, he still could not bear to part with this daughter.

Madame Zhang persuaded gently, "Why can't it be? They are both your flesh and blood. Since Qing Yan was originally supposed to marry, replacing her with the third girl seems acceptable to me. I am not being cruel as a grandmother. After all, it was Qingci who brought this shame upon herself. In that case, let her marry to the General's Manor in Qing Yan's place. It can be considered as the third girl making amends, and it can also restore some of the Duke's Manor's reputation. In the future, we can find another suitable marriage for Qing Yan, which can also bring more support to our Duke's Manor. Lord Duke, think carefully about it."

Yu Qingci stood quietly at the lower position, listening. When she finally heard Madame Zhang mention the words "substitute marriage," she could not help but sneer inwardly. She was willing to be a substitute, but not under the pretense of a tarnished reputation.

Before her father could speak, Yu Qingci said, "Do Grandmother and Father really intend to convict me of this crime based solely on this pouch?"

Madame Zhang shouted, "You still have the face to speak? Just now, several people testified that this pouch is yours. Do you still intend to deny it?"

Yu Qingci ignored Madame Zhang and stepped forward, pointing at the pouch. "This pouch is made of brocade, and the embroidery pattern is common. This style of pouch is not only mine; my second sister also has one. Just now, my second sister, fourth sister, and Siqin all said they had seen it with me. But I remember that on the first day I returned to the manor, my second sister was wearing a pouch just like this, and the color was also this tender yellow, isn't that right, Second Sister?"

Yu Qingci looked at Yu Qing Yan and continued, "So, can I also say that this pouch might belong to my second sister?"

"You're talking nonsense!" Yu Qing Ying could not help but blurt out.

Yu Qingci continued, "As for Young Master Jiao claiming that I personally had Tong’er give it to him, is there any proof? We can't just take his word for it. The reputation of the Duke's Manor's daughters is not so easily slandered."

Madame Qiao frowned, not expecting that even at this moment, this girl could remain so calm and dare to shift the blame onto her own daughter.

Qiao Yuantao quickly interjected, "Everything I said earlier is true. There is also a silk handkerchief inside the pouch, which should also belong to my third cousin."

Everyone's gaze shifted back to the pouch on the table. Qin Mom walked over, picked it up, opened it, and indeed took out a silk handkerchief, which she then unfolded for everyone to see.

The handkerchief was made of moon-white cloud brocade, embroidered with a few iris flowers in silk thread. The leaves were outlined with gold thread, making the colors appear particularly rich and vibrant.

Yu Qing Yan's expression changed instantly upon seeing the handkerchief.

Tong’er spoke up, "This handkerchief is not my mistress's. My mistress never embroiders flowers on her handkerchiefs. However, this iris pattern does look familiar. It seems that the second young lady likes this pattern. The second young lady's Ao also has irises embroidered on it."

---

chapters.title: Reversal
chapters.content:
Madame Qiao quickly took the handkerchief and examined it closely. The embroidered pattern on it was indeed an iris.

Everyone turned to look at Yu Qing Yan. Today, she was wearing a crimson Sichuan brocade Ao with a front opening, and the embroidered pattern on it was exactly the same as the one on the handkerchief—light purple irises with leaves outlined in gold thread.

Seeing everyone looking at her, Yu Qing Yan's expression immediately turned ugly. "Enough! The iris is just a common embroidery pattern. Besides, what I wear is none of your business, you lowly servant girl."

Yu Qingci said leisurely, "To my knowledge, not many people in the Duke's Manor use iris as an embroidery pattern. It seems only my second sister likes it. Moreover, most of my second sister's handkerchiefs are embroidered with irises, and the leaves are often outlined with gold thread."

Madame Qiao angrily said, "Shut up! How dare you tarnish your second sister's reputation?"

Madame Qiao was stunned by the sudden appearance of the handkerchief and felt a surge of resentment. Qing Yan had grown up in the manor, and everyone in the manor knew that the second young lady liked irises and often used iris patterns for her embroidery. Naturally, no one else would use the same pattern. Therefore, in the eyes of everyone in the Duke's Manor, the iris was unique to Yu Qing Yan.

Yu Jingcheng, of course, was also aware of this. At this moment, he frowned and took the handkerchief from Madame Qiao to examine it closely. Then he looked at Yu Qing Yan. "Take out your handkerchief."

Yu Qing Yan looked at her father in disbelief. "Father..."

Yu Jingcheng said sternly, "Take it out!"

Yu Qing Yan had no choice but to reluctantly take out her own handkerchief.

Yu Jingcheng took it and placed the two handkerchiefs side by side for comparison. His face darkened with anger as he threw both handkerchiefs at Madame Qiao. "Look for yourself. If this pouch belongs to Qingci, why does it contain Qing Yan's handkerchief?"

Madame Qiao glared fiercely at the dumbfounded Qiao Yuantao. Qiao Yuantao also seemed confused by the situation. His eyes darted around, not knowing what to do.

Madame Qiao pointed at Yu Qingci and said, "You, you actually..."

Yu Qingci's voice grew colder. "What have I actually done? Unless Madame is going to say that this handkerchief is also mine? I remember that my second sister's favorite is the iris. The clothes, handkerchiefs, and pouches that my second sister usually uses often have a few irises embroidered with gold-threaded leaves. If this is my second sister's belonging, it would make sense, given their close relationship as cousins."

Madame Zhang, Yu Qing Ying, and the others also realized that both handkerchiefs were indeed the kind that Yu Qing Yan usually used. Their expressions froze.

They were all close to Yu Qing Yan and naturally knew that she had liked iris flowers since she was a child. The pouches, handkerchiefs, and other items she usually carried often featured this pattern.

Yu Qing Ying was so angry that she jumped up and pointed at Yu Qingci. "I know now! It was you who deliberately embroidered a handkerchief identical to my second sister's to frame her. How vicious you are!"

Yu Qingci replied, "I have only just returned to the manor. How could I know my second sister's preferences so well, and go to the trouble of embroidering a handkerchief and involving your Jiao family's cousin to frame my second sister?"

"You..."

Yu Qing Ying, unable to argue, pointed at Qiao Yuantao. "And you! Where did you pick up this handkerchief? How dare you bring it here and make baseless accusations? This is definitely not my sister's handkerchief!"

Madame Qiao angrily shouted, "Silence! Of course this is not your second sister's thing."

Qiao Yuantao finally realized what had happened, but he had not expected such a turn of events. When Siqin had given him the pouch, he had quickly taken it and left. After returning, he had discovered the silk handkerchief inside and felt even more secure, thinking it was additional proof. He had never considered that there might be a mistake, so naturally, he had not thought to confirm it with Madame Qiao. Now, seeing how things had turned out, his face turned pale with fear, and his eyes darted around in panic. This was not how things were supposed to go. He silently cursed his luck.

He looked uncertainly at Madame Qiao, but under the watchful eyes of everyone, she could not say much and could only warn him with her eyes not to speak nonsense.

Qiao Yuantao gritted his teeth. "Two days ago, at the Shen hour, in the back garden."

Yu Qingci gave a cold laugh and looked at Yu Jingcheng again. "Father, you should remember that for these past two days, whenever you returned from outside, before the Shen hour, I would go to the study to bring you the tonic I made myself, and also to practice calligraphy with my brother. And each time, I was accompanied by Tong’er. We would stay until the You hour before returning to my own courtyard."

Yu Jingcheng recalled that this daughter was the most considerate. In the past, when they were in the countryside in Youyang, she often sent him tonics. These past few afternoons, when he had nothing to do, he would call Qingbai to the study to test his knowledge, and indeed, his daughter would always bring the tonic. Tong’er was always by her side, never leaving for a moment.

Yu Jingcheng, realizing this, looked at Qiao Yuantao with a fierce gaze. "You wretched thing, if you don't tell the truth now, don't blame me for being impolite. Come here!"

chapters.title: The End
chapters.content:
At the command, armed guards rushed out and surrounded Qiao Yuantao. Terrified, Qiao Yuantao cried out to Qiao-shi, "Aunt, save me!"

Qiao-shi tried to step forward to block, but Yu Jingcheng ignored her and ordered his men to seize Qiao Yuantao, drag him away, and give him a sound beating with a board. If he dared to implicate the daughter of the Nanping Earl, he would have to bear the consequences.

Soon, the crack of the board echoed from outside, but there was no sound from Qiao Yuantao—his mouth must have been gagged.

After all, he was her maternal relative, and Qiao-shi couldn’t bear to watch the Earl beat him to death. In a panic, she knelt before Zhang-shi and begged for mercy.

Zhang-shi stood up and persuaded, "Earl, stop. This matter must be clarified to silence the rumors. You’re too hasty. If you really beat him to death, it will be even harder to explain later. Besides, he is a young man from your in-laws’ family, a son of an innocent household. A few strikes as a lesson should suffice."

Yu Jingcheng calmed down and realized he couldn’t just beat the man to death. He ordered them to bring Qiao Yuantao back. In just a short time, Qiao Yuantao had already been beaten until his clothes were stained with blood, and he lay on the ground, unable to move.

Qiao-shi approached Qiao Yuantao and asked, "You foolish child! Where did you pick up that thing? Speak honestly at once! Do you have to wait until your uncle beats you to death like a thief before you’re satisfied?"

Qiao-shi didn’t dare to mention Yu Qingci now, so she could only prompt Qiao Yuantao.

Gritting his teeth against the pain, Qiao Yuantao followed Qiao-shi’s lead and said, "Yes, yes, I was muddle-headed for a moment. I picked up that pouch in the garden two days ago. At the time, I saw the one who dropped it seemed to be Young Lady Tong’er, so I had a moment of foolishness and harbored improper thoughts. Yuan'ao knows he was wrong. He shouldn’t have presumed to covet the Earl’s daughter. I deserve this beating and beg my uncle’s forgiveness."

At this moment, Yu Qingman’s personal wet nurse stepped forward and knelt before Yu Jingcheng, saying, "Earl, spare his life! It’s all this old slave’s fault. That day, I had just made a new pouch and handkerchief for the Second Young Lady, but before she could use them, they went missing. I must have carelessly dropped them when I went to the garden.

The Second Young Lady didn’t know about this. I thought I would just make new ones, but I never expected that Young Master Qiao would pick up the pouch and mistake it for the Third Young Lady’s. That’s how this disaster happened.

Just now, this old slave’s eyes were too dim to understand what was going on. I beg the Earl’s forgiveness and ask that you spare this old slave’s life."

Yu Jingcheng kicked her, and the wet nurse was sent flying, unable to get up for a long time.

Qiao-shi pointed at Qiao Yuantao and scolded, "I treated you as my own nephew, but you dared to covet the Earl’s daughters! It’s despicable! The Earl punishing you is only right. Only because you are my nephew am I sparing your life. But from now on, you are forbidden from setting foot in the Earl’s residence ever again!"

After saying this, she looked at Yu Jingcheng with a pleading gaze and murmured, "Earl, it’s my fault. I failed to discipline my relatives properly. Please calm your anger and don’t harm your health."

Yu Jingcheng said in a deep voice, "Today, Qingci has been wronged. You must comfort her properly. As for your nephew, you will personally send him back to your maiden home and explain everything to them. And Qingman’s wet nurse cannot stay in the residence any longer."

This was as much face as he could give Qiao-shi.

Qiao-shi didn’t dare say another word. She had someone take the wet nurse and Qiao Yuantao away and left with her two daughters.

The main hall quickly emptied. Yu Jingcheng beckoned Yu Qingci to his side, sighed, and said, "I’ve wronged you today. It’s all my fault as a father for being muddle-headed and almost believing others’ lies."

Yu Qingci hurried to comfort her father, "This isn’t your fault. It’s all that Qiao’s fault for being so wicked. If such a person were to pass the imperial examinations, it would be an injustice!"

Yu Jingcheng coldly scoffed, "Him? He can forget about ever taking the autumn imperial examinations."

How dare he frame the daughter of the Nanping Earl? Did he think it would be so easy to get away with?

Hearing her father say this, Yu Qingci felt a weight lift from her heart. She secretly thought to remind her father about the autumn examinations next year.

Zhang-shi also felt uncomfortable and said to the father and daughter, "I’m tired. You two should go rest as well if you have nothing else to do."

Yu Jingcheng personally escorted Yu Qingci back to the Wisteria Courtyard, said a few comforting words, and then left.

Qiao-shi ordered someone to temporarily settle Qiao Yuantao in the back courtyard. She didn’t dare to call a doctor for him. It was too late today, so she could only wait until tomorrow to send him back.

Since the Earl had ordered her to personally send him back, she didn’t dare disobey.

After arranging everything, Qiao-shi apologetically said to Qin Mom, who had followed her: "This is all my nephew’s fault for having improper thoughts. He disturbed the Old Madam. Tomorrow, I will personally go to the Old Madam to apologize. I beg you, Mom, to speak a few comforting words to the Old Madam on my behalf and not let her get angry and harm her health over this."

Qin Mom tactfully replied, "Madam, rest assured. This old slave will explain everything to the Old Madam. I will certainly not allow the reputations of the young ladies in the residence to be damaged. As for the servants involved tonight, I will strictly discipline them."

After Qin Mom left, Qiao-shi gritted her teeth and ordered her maid, Zhishu: "Go call that dead girl Siqin here."

She had originally thought to use this matter to ruin that lowly girl’s reputation. Once a young lady’s reputation was ruined, no good family would want her, and the idea of marrying into a noble family would be out of the question.

Once that lowly girl’s reputation was ruined, she could then bring up the matter of substituting the marriage to the Old Madam. The Old Madam would surely agree, and then the Old Madam could persuade the Earl, and the matter would be settled.

But now, not only had her plan failed, but her precious daughter’s reputation had also been tarnished. How could she not be furious?

Soon, Siqin arrived and knelt trembling before Qiao-shi, saying, "This slave did indeed see the Third Young Lady take off the pouch from her own body. When the Third Young Lady went inside to wash up, this slave took it. I absolutely did not make a mistake."

Qiao-shi: "Then what about the handkerchief in the pouch?"

Siqin shook her head repeatedly, "This slave truly doesn’t know. This slave was afraid of being discovered, so after taking the pouch, I immediately went to the back courtyard and gave it to Young Master Qiao. I never opened the pouch and didn’t know there was something inside. It’s all this slave’s fault for not handling the matter properly. I beg Madam’s forgiveness."

Seeing that she couldn’t get anything useful from Siqin, Qiao-shi angrily kicked her. Siqin’s face turned pale from the kick, but she gritted her teeth, got up, and continued kowtowing to beg for mercy.

Wu Mom beside her advised, "Madam, Siqin is one of our people and certainly wouldn’t help the Third Young Lady lie. But the Third Young Lady is only fifteen years old after all. How could she have such intricate thoughts? In this old slave’s opinion, it must have been that outsider’s idea. It seems they had long planned this vicious scheme against us."

Qiao-shi thought it over and could only conclude the same. She didn’t believe that a fifteen-year-old girl like Yu Qingci could come up with such a brilliant counterattack. The one helping her must be Su-shi.

---

chapters.title: Tai Jue Temple
chapters.content:
Qiao-shi: "If Siqin is telling the truth, then Su-shi and her daughter’s schemes run too deep. This time, we were careless. We thought she was just an inexperienced little girl, but we fell right into their trap and almost ruined my daughter’s reputation. This debt, I will settle with Su-shi slowly in the future."

Wu Mom: "Of course we can’t let them off so easily. Since this attempt failed, the matter of substituting the marriage is urgent. Why doesn’t this old slave go to Tai Jue Temple tomorrow to find Master Yuan Kong?"

Qiao-shi nodded, and the mistress and servant dismissed the maids to whisper privately.

In the Wisteria Courtyard, Yu Qingci returned to her room, bathed thoroughly, and finally felt a bit more comfortable. Tong’er entered quietly and said, "Young Lady, Siqin was just taken away."

Yu Qingci gave a cold smile. She didn’t care about Siqin’s fate. Since Qiao-shi and the others had failed in their scheme, they would naturally take out their anger on Siqin, the maid who had bungled the task.

As for herself, Qiao-shi would definitely not give up and would find another opportunity to force her into the substitute marriage. So she was in no hurry. She would wait for their next move.

Tong’er was extremely relieved they had escaped this disaster and couldn’t help but admire her young lady. "Young Lady, you’re amazing! How did you know they would frame you? And you even prepared a pouch and handkerchief identical to the Second Young Lady’s in advance? And you told me to wait for the right moment to tear the pouch in public, leaving them with no way to defend themselves!"

Yu Qingci smiled faintly. "That pouch wasn’t worth much. Siqin was at least a second-class maid from Madam’s side. Would she really covet such a small thing? If she stole it, she must have had another motive.

We don’t take the initiative to harm others, but we absolutely cannot allow others to harm us so easily. As for the handkerchief, it was just a precaution. If they hadn’t intended to harm me, it wouldn’t have been necessary."

In her past life, she had been sisters with Yu Qingman for a period of time and knew that Qingman liked irises. All the small accessories she carried had this pattern, so it wasn’t difficult for her to make an identical one.

As for the "Man" character on the pouch, it was to confirm that it belonged to Yu Qingman.

After today’s commotion, she had become an eyesore to Qiao-shi and her daughters. But it didn’t matter. As long as Qiao-shi was determined to have her substitute in marriage, she wouldn’t truly harm her.

Tong’er nodded in agreement. "You’re right, Young Lady. You’re so clever. That Qiao Yuantao was severely beaten by the Earl. He deserved it."

Yu Qingci recalled how, after the beating, Qiao Yuantao had looked at her with undisguised hatred. In her past life, when Qiao-shi and her daughters had failed, they had used this very tactic to frame her for having an affair with Qiao Yuantao. Faced with the so-called evidence, she had been unable to prove her innocence and was publicly convicted, then betrothed to Qiao Yuantao.

Her mother had argued with her father over this, and the rift between them had grown.

So today’s beating was just a small down payment. In this life, she would ensure Qiao Yuantao never had a chance to rise.

The next day, Wu Mom brought several servants with a box of jewelry, six bolts of fine brocade, and a box of the finest bird’s nest, saying it was to apologize to the Third Young Lady for the wrongful accusation the day before and to help her recover from the shock.

Yu Qingci graciously accepted the gifts and said a few words to smooth things over before Wu Mom left.

As for Zhang-shi, over the next two days when Yu Qingci went to pay her respects, things went much more smoothly. At the very least, Zhang-shi no longer criticized her indirectly, and Yu Qingman also pretended as if nothing had happened, treating her with even more sisterly affection. Only Yu Qingying couldn’t restrain herself and occasionally made snide remarks, which Yu Qingci paid no mind to.

One day, in the Shouyin Hall, Qiao-shi brought up the matter of the General’s residence.

"The General’s residence sent a letter saying that in two days, they will hold a memorial service at Tai Jue Temple for the two late generals. They want Qingman to attend so that the high monks of Tai Jue Temple can check the compatibility of the children’s birth dates again.

I was thinking, why not also bring Qingying and Qingci? Since Qingman won’t be staying in the residence much longer, it would be good for the sisters to spend more time together."

Zhang-shi replied listlessly, "Do as you see fit."

Qiao-shi looked at the sisters with a kind gaze. Naturally, Qingman and Qingying had nothing to say, and Yu Qingci went along with it, nodding. "I’ll follow Mother’s arrangements."

And so the matter was settled.

At dusk, Yu Qingci calculated the time when Yu Qingbai would return from the clan school. She wanted to go to the front courtyard to ask her brother about his first day, but she knew the Earl’s residence had many rules, and a young lady from the inner quarters couldn’t freely pass through the second gate. So she had Tong’er go to the front courtyard to find her brother and ask.

Tong’er received the order and left in a hurry, returning just as quickly. She reported that she had seen the Seventh Young Master return, and he seemed to be in a good mood. He mentioned that the teacher had assigned him work and that he would study hard that night.

Yu Qingci was somewhat reassured. In her memories, the bullying at school had only gradually appeared after Qingbai had been there for some time. At first, with their father keeping a close watch, those people hadn’t dared to provoke her brother easily. So for now, the most urgent matter was still on her end.

Tomorrow’s trip to Tai Jue Temple—she had important things to do.

Thinking of this, she ordered Tong’er: "Go find the book of chess manuals that my mother gave me last time. Bring it with us to Tai Jue Temple tomorrow."

When she had first come to the Earl’s residence, her mother, fearing that she and her brother would be mistreated, had packed dozens of large trunks filled with clothes, jewelry, and daily necessities they were used to. She and her father had spent a long time persuading her mother to leave some behind at the Su residence and only bring the essentials.

However, that chess manual was something she had specifically asked her mother for, and her mother had given it to her without a word.

"Yes, Young Lady."

Although she didn’t understand why her young lady needed to bring a chess manual to Tai Jue Temple, this didn’t stop her from firmly carrying out her young lady’s orders.

The next day, Yu Qingci woke up early, bathed, and dressed. Since they were going to a temple, she deliberately chose a plain, light gray dress, with a powder-blue lotus-patterned open-front jacket over it. Her jewelry was modest: only a pair of white jade begonia hairpins, two tortoiseshell hair clasps, and a pair of light pink pearl earrings.

Today, Qiao-shi was taking her two daughters, Yu Qingman and Yu Qingying, along with Yu Qingci. The rest were their personal maids and a few accompanying matrons.

The Earl’s residence had prepared three carriages. Qiao-shi and her two daughters took the first and most spacious one. Adding Yu Qingci would have made it crowded, so Yu Qingci, happy to separate from them, tactfully took the second carriage with Tong’er. The remaining maids and matrons squeezed into the third carriage.

Tai Jue Temple was built on Jiyun Mountain in the suburbs. Because it was not far from the capital, there was a constant stream of pilgrims, including many noble families who came to burn incense and make offerings. It was a famous and prosperous temple.

The Earl’s carriages stopped at the foot of the mountain. Beyond that, the path consisted entirely of large stone steps leading up, which the carriages couldn’t traverse.

Fortunately, Tai Jue Temple wasn’t built too high—it was only halfway up the mountain. Several pavilions had been constructed along the way for pilgrims to rest. Most people who came to burn incense would walk up as a sign of sincerity.

The group disembarked from the carriages and, surrounded by guards and servants, began the ascent step by step. Soon, the outline of Tai Jue Temple came into view.

chapters.title: The Memorial Service
chapters.content:
As soon as she stepped through the temple gates, she heard the steady, flowing chant of sutras echoing around her, mingled with the rich scent of sandalwood incense that filled the air, instantly making her feel as though she had entered sacred ground, her mind and spirit calming.

Today, the Ningyuan General’s Manor was holding a memorial service for two generals who had died young in battle. They had specially reserved a grand hall in the rear courtyard of Tai Jue Temple to minimize disturbances from other pilgrims.

"Has the old madam of the Ningyuan General’s Manor arrived yet?" Madame Qiao asked the guest-receiving monk. The monk pressed his palms together in greeting, murmured "Amitabha," and then replied, "The old madam has already arrived. She is currently in the rear hall, chanting sutras and lighting eternal lamps for the two generals. All the benefactors, please follow me."

The group followed the monk past several front halls and soon arrived at the rear hall where the service was being held.

The rear hall was as spacious as the ones in the front. Upon entering, they saw rows of monks in robes sitting neatly on either side, chanting in unison. The entire hall was filled with swirling sandalwood incense. In front of the central Bodhisattva statue, a few women were kneeling devoutly on prayer mats, bowing their heads.

Madame Qiao led Yu Qingyan and her two sisters forward without disturbing them. Instead, they knelt behind the women and began to pray and offer incense.

When everyone rose, the old madam of the Ningyuan General’s Manor, Madame Ning, turned around with the help of her daughter. She saw Madame Qiao with a few young girls standing behind her. Her lips moved slightly, but no sound came out.

Yu Qingci looked up and saw that Madame Ning was dressed in light, plain clothing, her face filled with sorrow. Beside her stood a girl of about thirteen or fourteen, her gaze toward them carrying a hint of curiosity. These two were the mother-in-law and younger sister-in-law of her legitimate elder sister from her past life.

The joyous news of victory had arrived, followed immediately by the tragic news of their deaths. In a single night, Madame Ning had lost her husband and son, the two people closest to her. The once-illustrious general’s manor was now left with only an old woman and a weak girl to uphold the family name. Even with the honor bestowed by the imperial court, how long could this glory sustain them as time passed?

Thus, the general’s manor had insisted on marrying a daughter from the Nanping Marquis’s Manor, seeking long-term protection.

Madame Qiao stepped forward to console Madame Ning, then called her daughters to greet her.

Yu Qingyan was the first to step forward and bow gracefully. Madame Ning hurriedly moved to support her, but her eyes darted away, unable to meet Yu Qingyan’s gaze.

Her son was already gone, yet she had, under the urging of her clan, demanded that a young girl in the prime of her life marry into their family to spend a lifetime in widowhood. Madame Ning knew she was in the wrong.

Madame Qiao’s face showed a gentle expression, but with a trace of cold smirk as she watched Madame Ning’s guilty and uneasy demeanor before them.

After Qingyan finished her greetings, Madame Qiao spoke to Madame Ning: "Madam, please restrain your grief. The dead cannot be brought back to life. You must still plan for the future of the general’s manor and take care of your health.

Upon receiving your invitation, I brought Qingyan and my other daughters here. Besides offering incense and prayers for the young general and the great general, I also wanted to see you. Once Qingyan marries into your family, we will be one family, and naturally, we must take care of each other."

Madame Ning was deeply moved. With a hoarse voice, she said, "To be able to marry a good daughter-in-law like Qingyan is the fortune of our Lu family. Rest assured, once Qingyan marries in, I will cherish her as my own daughter and never let her suffer the slightest grievance."

Madame Qiao thought to herself with a cold smirk: *You forced my daughter to marry into your family to spend her life as a widow. How dare you say you won’t let her suffer?*

Yet, on the surface, she continued to console Madame Ning gently, then called Qingying and Qingci to greet her as well.

Madame Ning had not met Qingci before, but in recent days, rumors had spread among the high-ranking families that the Nanping Marquis’s Manor had taken in two children from an external concubine to recognize their ancestry. Presumably, this girl was one of them.

These rumors in the capital were mostly spread by Madame Qiao’s people, and naturally, they did not clarify the true identities of Yu Qingci and her brother, so up to this point, many people still believed they were the children of the Marquis’s concubine.

Madame Ning was in the midst of her grief and had no time to pay attention to other matters. So she only glanced at the two girls, gave a few perfunctory compliments, and then, without forgetting, removed a jade bracelet from her wrist and placed it in Yu Qingci’s hand.

"A small gift, take it and play with it."

Yu Qingci looked up at Madame Qiao, who nodded in approval before she thanked her and accepted it.

After a few pleasantries, the monks in the hall had prepared for the day’s memorial service. A monk draped in a kasaya, with a half-white beard, appeared before the crowd. He was Master Yuan Kong, who would preside over today’s service.

Madame Qiao stepped forward and bowed deeply to Master Yuan Kong: "Master, my daughter has personally copied some sutras and intends to burn them for the two generals today. I hope it won’t be too much trouble for you."

As she spoke, she signaled Yu Qingyan to step forward.

Yu Qingyan placed a thick stack of sutras on the incense table. Master Yuan Kong nodded and said, "Amitabha. The young benefactress’s sincerity is touching. This old monk will certainly do his best."

The service began. Master Yuan Kong sat cross-legged at the front, closed his eyes, and began to chant the sutras softly. As his voice gradually rose, the monks on either side also began to chant loudly.

Yu Qingci subtly moved to the spot closest to the temple door and knelt behind the crowd. She knew this service would last a long time, so she did not intend to kneel there the entire time.

She signaled to Tong’er, who was kneeling behind her. The two of them quietly shifted their legs outward, moving step by step toward the door until they were almost at the entrance. Then they stood up and silently slipped out of the hall.

Yu Qingying, kneeling behind Madame Qiao, also looked rather impatient. She simply could not endure such occasions.

Bored, she turned her head around and caught sight of Yu Qingci sneaking out. Her eyes widened, and without a second thought, she followed suit and slipped out as well.

Unfortunately, she was a step too late. By the time she left the hall, Yu Qingci’s figure was already out of sight. She stomped her foot in frustration.

"How dare that little wretch sneak out! I’ll catch her and give her a good scolding!" Yu Qingying gritted her teeth.

The maidservant following closely behind her ventured, "But, Third Young Lady, she’s already out of sight. Why don’t we go back inside and tell Madame? Then Madame can send someone to find Third Young Lady, and we can mock her properly."

Yu Qingying shot the maid a glare. "Can’t you see they’re busy with the service inside? How can we tell Mother now? Besides, we have time to find her ourselves.

Hmph, just now, Madame Ning was even praising her for being chaste, quiet, and virtuous. The service had just begun, and she’s already slipped away. Who knows where she’s wandered off to? If she bumps into some rough, uncouth men outside, it’ll bring shame to our Nanping Marquis’s Manor!"

Yu Qingying looked around, deciding that Yu Qingci had likely gone to the front halls, where there were more pilgrims, to watch the commotion. So she decided to search in that direction.

The maidservant dared not disobey her young mistress, so she followed closely behind as they walked forward.

Yu Qingci, with Tong’er, exited the hall and immediately followed the path she remembered toward the rear courtyard of the temple.

---

chapters.title: The Great Scholar
chapters.content:
Soon, they reached the temple’s rear gate. After informing the guest-receiving monk on duty, they exited through the back gate. Passing a few forks in the path shaded by bamboo groves, they followed the mountain trail forward. Before long, they could see several independent small courtyards built along the mountain path, nestled among the trees.

Quickly, they arrived in front of one of the courtyards.

From the outside, this courtyard looked similar to the neighboring ones—gray bricks, dark tiles, and lush green trees surrounding it.

Today, her main purpose in coming to Tai Jue Temple with Madame Qiao was to meet the person living in this courtyard.

She approached and knocked on the door. After a moment, the door opened, and a young servant stood before them.

"Who are you looking for?" the servant asked.

Yu Qingci replied politely, "Forgive the disturbance. I am the third young lady of the Nanping Marquis’s Manor. I’ve come specifically to visit Mr. Li, who resides here."

"He is not in," the servant said, about to close the door.

Yu Qingci quickly added, "I’ve heard that Mr. Li enjoys playing chess. Today, we’ve brought our family’s inherited chess manual to sincerely seek an audience. Given our sincerity, might we trouble you to announce our visit?"

The servant’s gaze fell on the chess manual in her hands but did not reach for it. Instead, he looked her and her maid up and down before saying, "Eight out of ten people who come to visit my master say the same thing. Most of them are men, though. It’s rare to have a young lady like you. But my master truly does not receive guests."

Yu Qingci immediately understood the servant’s implication—Mr. Li was at home but simply did not wish to see visitors.

She had already anticipated this, so she said, "I’ve heard that Mr. Li is so fond of chess that he’s obsessed with it. Today, I sincerely wish to present this chess manual to him. How can you know he doesn’t want to see it without asking him?"

The servant saw that she was still persistent. He had dealt with many such people before, but today, he was faced with a delicate young lady, and he couldn’t bring himself to be cold. So he frowned, looked at the chess manual in her hands, and said, "Alright, wait a moment. I’ll go announce your visit."

With that, he closed the door.

Yu Qingci and Tong’er waited quietly for a while before the servant opened the door again.

"My master is not free at the moment, but he invites the two young ladies inside for some tea."

With that, he stepped aside to let them in.

The servant led them to a grape trellis in the courtyard. Beneath it was a stone table and stone stools, with an unfinished game of Go laid out on the table.

The servant said, "Wait here. Please do not wander around, or the old master might get angry and drive you out."

Qingci quickly nodded in agreement.

After the servant left, he walked past the main hall to the back courtyard. The back courtyard was about an acre in size, most of which had been cultivated into a vegetable garden. An old man in coarse, short clothing was squatting in the garden, holding a small hoe, digging at the soil one stroke at a time.

The servant picked up a watering can from the edge of the field and began watering the other end. The two worked silently until they finished tending to one row of the garden.

Only then did the old man stand up, examining his work with satisfaction before stepping out of the garden.

"Master, the two young ladies are still waiting in the front courtyard," the servant reminded softly.

The old man, unhurried, washed his hands in a stone-built pool nearby before standing up and saying, "I’ll go take a look."

Yu Qingci and Tong’er sat under the grape trellis. As they waited, they grew bored and began counting the pieces on the Go board in front of them. Hearing footsteps approaching, they looked up and saw someone coming. They quickly stood up respectfully and said, "This junior greets Elder Mr. Li."

Mr. Li stood with his hands behind his back, his gaze sweeping over the young girl before him. She looked to be about fourteen or fifteen, with a clean and refreshing appearance that was rather pleasing.

However, in all these years, he had never taken on a female student, so he would still have to politely send her away after a while.

"Sit," Mr. Li said, gesturing for Yu Qingci to sit while he casually took a seat on the stone stool on the other side. His eyes fell on the stone table, and in an instant, Li Shen’s eyes widened as he leaned down to study the board intently.

He looked up at Yu Qingci in disbelief, then back at the board, repeating this several times before finally confirming that the game he had left unfinished for so long had been solved.

"Did you solve this?" Mr. Li asked uncertainly, pointing at the board.

Yu Qingci smiled and nodded. "This junior grew bored while waiting, so she took the liberty of making a move. Please forgive her presumption."

This was an indirect admission that she had solved the game.

Mr. Li could not help but re-examine the young girl before him.

"Your servant mentioned you are from the Nanping Marquis’s Manor?"

Yu Qingci replied, "Yes, this junior is the third young lady of the Nanping Marquis’s Manor. Today, I came to seek a tutor for my younger brother, Yu Qingbai. Mr. Li’s great name is renowned throughout the court and the land. My mother and father both hope that my brother will have the opportunity to study under you. As a token of our sincerity, my mother ordered me to present you with our family’s inherited chess manual."

Mr. Li took the chess manual and flipped through it quickly before setting it aside. His attention remained on the Go board in front of him, and a satisfied smile gradually appeared on his face.

"Come, come, young lady. Tell me how you solved this move. Why did you decide to place your stone here?" Mr. Li beckoned Yu Qingci to sit across from him, his manner much warmer now.

Over the years, many young prodigies had sought to become his disciples, and among them, some were skilled at Go. But none had been able to solve this game—let alone a young lady. This was the first.

By the time Yu Qingci left, half an hour had passed. Mr. Li had agreed to meet her brother another day to assess whether he would accept him as a student.

With Mr. Li’s preliminary approval, Yu Qingci was already greatly relieved.

In her past life, her husband, Qiao Yuantao, had once hoped to study under Mr. Li. From Qiao Yuantao, Yu Qingci had heard many stories about Mr. Li. She knew that he was a man of unparalleled status among scholars, with a noble background.

Mr. Li was a renowned scholar of vast learning, once serving as the Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince. After the prince ascended the throne, Mr. Li requested retirement and returned to a life of seclusion, living the idyllic existence described in the poem: "Plucking chrysanthemums by the eastern fence, leisurely I see the southern hills."

Over the years, countless scholars had come seeking to study under him, and many noble families had arrived with generous gifts, but Mr. Li, born into a prestigious family himself, had always disdained wealth. At his age, he sought only peace of mind, which was why he had left the bustling capital to live in this quiet place, enjoying a life of leisure like a wild crane among the clouds.

Thus, the number of students Mr. Li had accepted over the years was exceedingly small.

chapters.title: A Change in Destiny
chapters.content:
Yu Qingci knew it would be difficult to impress Old Master Li, so she thought of the idea of presenting him with chess manuals to see if it would appeal to his interests.

Old Master Li rarely formally accepted disciples, and his criteria for taking students were different from those of other great Confucian scholars. He mostly relied on first impressions—if a student caught his fancy, regardless of their background, he would be willing to accept them.

Unfortunately, since his retirement, although scholars had been coming to visit him in an endless stream, very few had truly caught his eye and been accepted as disciples.

For a period, Qiao Yuantao had been scheming about how to get close to Old Master Li. At that time, she had also been eager to help her husband, and had almost always complied with Qiao Yuantao’s financial demands.

From Qiao Yuantao, she had learned that Old Master Li was a chess fanatic with deep knowledge of the game. To keep out the endless stream of visitors, Old Master Li had set up a difficult chess puzzle, declaring that only those who could solve it would be worthy of drinking and conversing with him.

At first, a few masters had managed to solve Old Master Li’s chess puzzle. Later, in a fit of anger, he had set up an even more difficult one, and indeed, for a long time, no one had been able to solve it.

But she knew that in a few months, a young scholar named Zhou Jing would solve the puzzle. Zhou Jing would then be fortunate enough to be favored by Old Master Li and become his last accepted disciple.

Under Old Master Li’s guidance, Zhou Jing would pass the imperial examinations two years later, be personally selected by the current emperor as the second highest scholar, and then, riding on the reputation of being Old Master Li’s last disciple, quickly establish himself in the imperial court, enjoying great prestige.

What made scholars across the land envious was that this man was later favored by the Prime Minister, who took him as a son-in-law.

This should have been a life of great joy, but who could have known that three years later, Zhou Jing’s original wife would bring their young child to the capital to find him, revealing that he had already been married with a child in his hometown.

The Prime Minister’s daughter was a wise and understanding woman. Upon seeing her husband’s original wife, she resolutely divorced him and returned to her maiden home. When the Prime Minister learned the truth, he flew into a rage. Overnight, Zhou Jing went from being the nation’s darling to the target of public condemnation. Censoring officials repeatedly impeached him, and the emperor issued a decree banishing him to a remote post.

Who could have predicted that a few years later, Zhou Jing would become the most corrupt official in the region? After being reported, he was imprisoned. Only then did people learn that his original wife and child had been abandoned by him after his banishment, their fate unknown. Old Master Li, implicated by his disciple, had nearly suffered a ruin of both reputation and life, ultimately dying in frustration and sorrow.

At that time, the chess puzzle Zhou Jing had solved attracted much attention in the capital. Many scholars and Go masters studied the puzzle repeatedly, and Yu Qingci had been fortunate enough to see it and memorized it.

In this life, she would be the one to solve it.

Having resolved a major issue, Yu Qingci felt a sense of relief and satisfaction. She and her maid silently retraced their steps back to the rear hall, just in time to see the monks who had been performing the ritual filing out one by one.

Was it already over?

Yu Qingci secretly rejoiced that she had returned in time.

She stopped and stepped aside, waiting for the monks to pass before entering the rear hall with her maid.

Inside, she heard Qiao’s family surrounding Master Yuan Kong, their voices raised in what seemed like an emotional discussion.

Qiao’s voice, tinged with disbelief, carried over: "How could this be the result? When our two families arranged the marriage, we specifically sent the children’s birth charts to the temple for Master to verify, and he said it was a match made in heaven. How has it now become the worst possible choice?"

Master Yuan Kong’s deep, resonant voice carried a note of helplessness: "This old monk personally matched the birth charts of the young general and Miss Yu. Indeed, they showed a heavenly match. But now, their destinies have shifted—this is the will of heaven. If the two families disregard this and insist on the marriage, it may bring misfortune and even disaster to both families’ fortunes, possibly even affecting the longevity of the elders. I urge the ladies to reconsider."

Qiao looked at Old Madam Ning. The old lady’s face also showed disbelief: "How could this be? Could it be that after my son died for the country, he is now doomed to be alone, with no one to offer sacrifices to him?"

Master Yuan Kong pressed his palms together and continued to console: "Do not grieve, benefactor. The result of my divination is that Miss Yu’s destiny has changed, and she can no longer match with the young general’s spirit. This does not mean others cannot. The rise and fall of connections are all cause and effect. Everything has its destiny; the benefactor should accept it naturally."

Qiao’s eyes lit up: "Does Master mean there is another woman who can marry the young general?"

Master Yuan Kong’s expression remained inscrutable: "Amitabha. The young general is a man of great merit. Heaven has its own arrangements."

Yu Qingci, upon hearing this, could not help but curl her lips into a mocking smile. Here it comes.

In her past life, after the ritual, Qiao had pretended to take out Yu Qingwan’s birth chart and asked Master Yuan Kong to divine her future. The monk, after some calculations, had declared that destiny had changed and the two could not marry.

Now, thinking back, wasn’t this all arranged by Qiao? This so-called enlightened monk was just taking money to dispel misfortune for others.

Qiao seemed to notice Yu Qingci’s entrance and asked: "Qingci, why have you returned from outside? Where did you go just now?"

Everyone turned to look. Yu Qingchen was the first to rush forward and question: "Yu Qingci, while everyone was performing the ritual, you dared to sneak out and wander around. How bold of you! Tell me, where did you go, and why are you only back now?"

Yu Qingci looked up and saw that Yu Qingchen’s face was flushed with anger, and there were traces of tears. Looking at her clothes, the hem of the goose-yellow dress with embroidered butterflies that she had worn that morning was stained with dirt, and her overall appearance was disheveled.

What had happened?

Yu Qingwan saw this and stepped forward to block between them, gently asking Yu Qingci: "Third sister, why did you leave without a word? You didn’t even bring a servant with you. What if someone had bumped into you?"

Yu Qingci calmly explained: "I felt a bit dizzy earlier and didn’t want to disturb everyone during the ritual, so I just went to the bamboo forest pavilion at the back and didn’t go far. I didn’t mean to worry you, Aunt and Second Sister."

Qingchen’s eyes widened again upon hearing this: "You went to the back courtyard? No wonder I couldn’t find you after searching the front courtyard for so long. You really have no sense of propriety! Everyone was here listening to Master’s ritual, but you faked being dizzy just to sneak out and wander around!"

Yu Qingci looked at the two sisters with an apologetic tone: "It was my fault. I should have told Aunt. But, what happened to Fourth Sister?"

Yu Qingci deliberately looked Yu Qingchen up and down with a suspicious expression.

Yu Qingchen, with a cry in her voice, said: "How dare you ask me? If it weren’t for you, I wouldn’t have..."
